Super value unlimited everything at the price of 66aed +++
We had a great Easter Sunday lunch
*Unlimited hotpot soup with all the ingredients noodles, beef and chicken  meat, veggies,  etc
With cooking pot refillable soup and ingredients
*Yummy dimsums dumplings
*Siopao or white buns
* Desserts ice cream, buchi
* Drinks lemongrass iced tea.
Some of the favorites are
Toasted chicken
Spring rolls
Chicken feet
Steamed dimsums and dumpling served in bamboo style
Dumplings are Seafood, chicken ,beef
Vegetables

We weren't able to try..maybe next time the following
Red ice tea
Milk tea
Takoyaki
Pad Thai
Rice bowls

Corn dog cheesey
Now after coming home, I finally miss having the buffet and eating everything. The food were delicious.
One of the Value for money finds in Dubai.
They have many branches discovery gardens and deira.
They are also available to do ala carte if you don't want unlimited.
The place has outdoor dining and ample.parking paid parking though.
It's in cluster X of JLT, I'm just not sure bout the other branches.
As for the order system...it can improve because our list got lost and we were waiting for our order. Also the place has lots of customers hope bigger space.
Overall very satisfied with asian super bowl.  Real deal.

A fantastic restaurant in the base of the Atlantis, The Palm. Being adjacent to the aquarium with connecting walls, offers the most amazing ambience for the restaurant, although the food speaks to the quality of the place at an even higher level. The French Chef, Greg, has painstakingly created a menu that is as theatrical and interesting as it is tasty. Every dish is pinned to a memory of his as he has travelled through life and this is laid out on a menu that is represented as a map of France. The unexpected and surprising occurs frequently throughout the set menu dining experience. If lucky, you will catch the chef for a chat as he frequents the dining area to check on his guests. We are wishing Greg all the best in hopefully obtaining two Michellin stars in a couple of weeks, which would beat his already one. This is a dining experience not to be missed if you are in Dubai and I put this as one of the worlds bests. Highly recommend.

Every dish is pinned to a memory of his as he has travelled through life and this is laid out on a menu that is represented as a map of France. The unexpected and surprising occurs frequently throughout the set menu dining experience. If lucky, you will catch the chef for a chat as he frequents the dining area to check on his guests. We are wishing Greg all the best in hopefully obtaining two Michellin stars in a couple of weeks, which would beat his already one. This is a dining experience not to be missed if you are in Dubai and I put this as one of the worlds bests. Highly recommend.

We had a phenomenal experience at Hakkasan, thanks to our amazing server, Soe.
We started with the boneless Peking duck, which was perfectly crispy on the outside and tender inside, bursting with rich flavors that set the tone for the meal. For the main course, we had the Peking duck with bone, which was equally delicious and expertly prepared, offering a deeper, more robust flavor. The stir-fry veggies were fresh and crisp, perfectly seasoned, complementing the richness of the duck. The hand-pulled noodles were a highlight, with a perfect texture and delightful taste that paired wonderfully with the other dishes.
We finished the meal with their famous spiked lemon, a refreshing and tangy dessert that was the perfect end to our meal, and Chinese tea, which was aromatic and soothing, recommended by Soe. The experience truly felt like a Michelin-star experience because of Soe's exceptional service and attention to detail. We left feeling valued and well taken care of. Highly recommend giving Hakkasan a try for an unforgettable dining experience!

I was totally excited to finally have the opportunity to try out this well-known franchise during my trip to Abu Dhabi.
Making my reservation was easy - I made mine via google map and got it confirmed immediately.
The location of the restaurant was pretty odd - it’s located down a long corridor after a bank branch, and three souvenir shops within the large Emirates Mall; one wouldn’t expect a high end restaurant to be located near these.
Service was within my expectations. However I rated this a 3-star as all my dim-sum was brought out immediately before I could even start to finish a bite. This meant that (1) my table was filled to the max (2) my food got cold before I could even try it (3) visually, it made me so full
Food was also within my expectations but nothing spectacular. Nothing out of the ordinary that a dim sum restaurant in Singapore could not make.
Would I return? Yeah maybe..  but I would not give it a Michelin star.

This is my first time to have premium Chinese cuisine in Abu Dhabi.
First, the staff, they’re really helpful to explain every dishes that we ordered from the menu.
For the atmosphere, maybe I’m not really used with eating in the dark, so it’s just a bit too dark for me.
The premium dim sum is amazing! Especially the one with truffle!
My favourite its the shrimp roll! They’re so good! The sauce is savory and sweet, perfect match with the crispy skin from shrimp roll!
The rice (i believe it was a mix brown, white and black rice) was lightly seasoned, eating the rice itself is already delicious for me. The wagyu beef came with crispy mushroom, the sauce is sweet and savory, perfect pair with the rice.
For the dessert, i like the spiky lemon cake! So tangy and sour yet sweetest is also there!
Overall it was an amazing experience!

Never underestimate the impact of word of mouth marketing, because the sheer number of people that said I must try Kinoya was overwhelming! With good reason, the ramen ranks among the top 3 I've ever tried. Long lines outside ramen places are no indicator of quality, but I can see why Kinoya requires advance reservations.
We went with the Spicy Miso and Shio Paitan, and with both, the broth was flavorful and the meat was tender, the dish came to the table piping hot - as it should! The noodles weren't clumpy or rubbery, just the right texture to complement the ingredients in the bowl. And I appreciate the option to choose between two sizes, most ramen places default to a single large size.
This was accompanied by Burnt Butter Scallops, which were a first for me and I can confidently say, it'll be hard for anyone to top this: perfectly cooked with a rich flavor and a sauce that wasn't cloying, it was an unexpected winner!
It doesn't need to be your first foray into Japanese cuisine, but even if it is, Kinoya comes highly recommended, and lives up to the promise.

Situated in Abu Dhabi mall, Bosphorus is a well known Turkish restaurant serving exotic dishes, at exotic prices.
Their food is really exotic and sumptuous, and presentation is amazing.

It’s best to order 2 dishes at a time for 3 people.
Place is on the expensive side.
Vegetarian options: Not sure, but noticed veg stuff too.

Based on the great food at the JLT brunch, I was looking forward to taking my husband to a pizza express brunch for the first time for his birthday. Unfortunately, it was below average.
The waiter who seated us did not note my name just asked if we had a booking so I’m assuming didn’t bother to check the birthday note I’d made on the booking. There was no acknowledgment of his birthday. However the table next to us, maybe friends of the staff or the singers as they were very friendly, were given cake, candles and a song.
There were 3 tables at brunch so I’m surprised at the lack of attentiveness as they were not busy at all.
Food: all could have been forgiven if the food had been delicious. For a pizza restaurant and brunch, only 4 pizzas to choose from seems a bit lazy. And only one with meat on. And one with prawns, I wonder how many people order prawn pizza…
We were really disappointed with this, based on the choice of the normal menu. I think if the brunch menu was obvious on the website, we wouldn’t have booked.
With the lack of choice, there was also lack of flexibility. We asked for pepperoni (beef) to be added to the picante which was free of charge but if we wanted to add chicken to the Quattro it was extra charge.
When the pizzas came, the flavours were dull. The dough was heavy. A lot of red onion.
Starters were basic, we enjoyed the chicken bites. The honey dough balls were an attempt at re-designing the classic garlic dough balls. Weird spicy bread, which we did not enjoy. We saw another table had the classic dough balls so we were relieved there was no extra charge for these to be brought out as part of our starters.
The pizza we saw being delivered to tables outside the brunch, looked very different and appetizing.
Dessert: we didn’t want any but we weren’t offered the option to order any.
Cocktails were weak and watery.
The Bubblegum/prosecco/orange juice was so sickly sweet, it was like something an amateur bar tender would make. Due to the lack of choice, we stuck with vodka/Pepsi and beer.
I would have expected better tables service as they were so quiet, rather having to keep asking for another round of the same drinks.
Entertainment: very loud sound check and instrument tuning one hour into the brunch was disruptive and annoying. Why didn’t they do that before the brunch started?
From a price point, it’s a very good deal. But if the food isn’t good, it’s not enough to make you want to return.
Note for management: marketing is abysmal. Your website online form gave no confirmation of booking.
Had to go to socials and tried via WhatsApp, which then took me to Table Agent. With three different booking routes to attempt to get a table, and the brunch being so average, this was a really disappointing experience. Maybe this is why you only had 3 tables.
In short, we wouldn’t return or recommend.

Dishes like the Hakka handpulled noodles do contain egg but are not labeled correctly in the menu (so we were told by our server). All in all, decent food, but the experience is far from European Michelin star standards.
Vegetarian options: Plenty of veggie, few vegan ones.

My husband and I came here for our anniversary meal and were bitterly disappointed.
The restaurant wasn’t very busy on the particular weekend that we were there so managed to walk in without a reservation whilst visiting the Palace. The decor and ambience was impressive, I loved the dark and moody interiors. The screens made every area feel private and intimate, and the staff were friendly and helpful.
We ordered the amaretti sour and tropical club mocktails. They were delicious and so well balanced. For starters, we ordered the prawn fritters with truffle, which were crunchy and delicious. However, the main course is where the disappointment started. We had the sweet and sour chicken with pomegranate, which was tasteless and over cooked. The lamb two ways was also disappointing. One was undercooked and tasted like grass, and the other part was really over cooked, and again, very bland and tasteless.
Very disappointed with our experience, and probably won’t be returning. I expect better food for this price. We were expecting much better than this from a restaurant with a Michelin star!

However, the main course is where the disappointment started. We had the sweet and sour chicken with pomegranate, which was tasteless and over cooked. The lamb two ways was also disappointing. One was undercooked and tasted like grass, and the other part was really over cooked, and again, very bland and tasteless.
Very disappointed with our experience, and probably won’t be returning. I expect better food for this price. We were expecting much better than this from a restaurant with a Michelin star!

Yesterday (16.05.2024) evening, I visited The Cheesecake Factory with my friends. During our meal, I noticed something was snagging my shirt on the chair. We had a great time, paid our bill, and left. However, in the next store, I saw that my shirt was covered in pulls and completely ruined. I returned to the restaurant and showed it to the manager, Ahmed.
His initial reaction was to say that all their chairs are smooth and he couldn't believe this happened. Eventually, he offered me a piece of cake, probably for free, but we were too full to eat anything else. He didn't offer any other solution, though I would have accepted a voucher for a future visit. Unfortunately, such an offer was not made, and the evening was ruined.
I was disappointed with the way this situation was handled. I hope the restaurant improves its customer service and attention in the future.

column9: We visited Spice Grill as 2 in late February after passing by it multiple times and finding it an appealing prospect to try out. I must say it did not disappoint and is in fact our new favorite destination for seafood in the UAE. The restaurant is located in the scenic Majaz Waterfront overlooking the corniche which makes for a great view. I would also like to especially appreciate and thank Hamfrey who went the extra mile in being very attentive and polite and also helped us to make the right order for our mood and respective palates. We chose to get the Cajun Shrimp with extra spice, Cheese Baked Mussels, Grilled Squid, Chicken Wings in dynamite and Garlic Parmesan flavors and Iced Tea. The servings on all the dishes were large and the cajun shrimp was easy to peel and deliciously extra spicy as requested, had us reaching for the tissue box often. Mussels were large and cheesy and left a lasting taste!  Food, ambiance and service were nothing short of spectacular and we would definitely be visiting again soon 😊

🌟 🌟 Mama'esg DIFC Central Park is an absolutely amazing place! If you visit, make sure to sit outside and enjoy the stunning view of the Burj Khalifa 🌇. Just a heads up, this is best enjoyed during the cooler winter months ❄️, as the summer heat can be quite intense ☀️.

I have several allergies, and although they were about to close, the staff went above and beyond to prepare a special dinner tailored to my dietary needs 🥗🍽️. Their dedication and attentiveness left a lasting impression, and I will definitely be returning again and again!
The ambiance at Mama'esg is charming and relaxing, perfect for unwinding after a long day 🛋️. The outdoor seating area provides a lovely setting to enjoy your meal while taking in the iconic skyline views 🌃. The staff are incredibly friendly and accommodating, making you feel right at home 🏠.
Mama'esg DIFC Central Park offers not just great food but an unforgettable dining experience. The combination of the beautiful view, fantastic service, and delicious meals makes it a must-visit spot in Dubai. I highly recommend this place for anyone looking for a delightful dining experience 🌟🍴🌆.

Chagh Kabob Turkish restaurant has a lot of heart and character. The owners were on site to greet customers, taking pleasure to get to know customers. They made us feel welcome, special and at home.
Our dining party was six and we were wrapping up our eid celebrations. We made a reservation and recommend you do also since the place isn’t very big. The menu was clear and concise, consisting of some light breakfast items and a collection of grills.
The food was delicious.They served a variety of fresh warm breads alongside tender juicy and flavorful grills. The salads were lightly dressed and perfectly balanced with fresh ingredients. We added The Turkish Breakfast for four to get a feel for the breadth and depth of the menu. All was prepared with great care.
This is their new location and if you go soon you can avail the 50% off promotion. Six of us feasted for less than 450 dirham. A truly spectacular value for the exceptional food and warm service we received.
Don’t hesitate, give it a try.

My first few experiences of the cheesecake factory haven’t been great, but this one differed. The staff were welcoming and friendly, and gave us really helpful tips on what to order and how much to order.
To start with, the portions here are HUGE so although they weren’t doing the lunch menu in the evening, they did a lunch size Louisiana chicken pasta for me. This was still very big and I couldn’t finish it. The chicken was crispy and the flavours of the pasta were delicious. We also ordered the factory Turkey burger that came with chips, and again the portion was very large. I would suggest ordering small plates to share for small eaters like me.
We left some room for dessert, so we then had the Adam’s peanut butter cup fudge ripple which we managed to finish off. This was delicious, creamy and full of flavour.
Very reasonable prices for the food portions and choices. Great for a family outing!

I came to Cheesecake Factory with the same expectations that I always have - A cozy atmosphere, giant portions of food, and the lovely service. On my latest visit here, the place checked out all three of these expectations, however I must say that the BBQ burger was really dry. I ordered the Cherry Limeade which was sharp, tangy and sweet, the Louisiana Chicken Pasta which was creamy, spicy, and delicious, but the BBQ burger was disappointing. The patty was cooked to the point where the BBQ sauce could not even rehydrate it. There was too much bun and onion rings, but i wish the patty was medium well instead of beyond well done. The fries and the barbecue dipping sauce were delicious though. Our server, Marie Grace did a phenomenal job of keeping us engaged and ensuring we were well-fed. Obviously this was a case of one order gone south, but will definitely visit Cheesecake Factory again. Also, please open a branch in Sharjah 😉
Parking: There is a parking lot inside the mall.

On our visit to Al Ain during the Eid Al Adha holidays as we were searching for good Indian cuisine restaurants, we casually came across this restaurant named CORIANDER with a high rating in google search and so we decided to explore.
CORIANDER has both inside sitting arrangement for those who need privacy and outside court sitting for others who enjoy food in the open.
We were greeted and guided to our table by the most courteous staff Chetan. Chetan was personally attentive to make us comfortable and suggested us the most palatable food combinations we should try.
As a welcome drink we were offered a complimentary shot of pineapple juice with subtle spices in fuming dry ice.
In starters we ordered mix vegetable platter followed by crispy okra with mix vegetables and mozarella cheese and garlic naan as an accompaniment in the main course. The strawberry mojito had a unique fresh taste lingering in the mouth and our first gastronomical journey with CORIANDER ended with soft succulent gulab jamuns which melted in our mouths.
On another occasion,  we repeated veg platter, crispy okra with mix vegetables and also ordered butter chicken coins, chicken hyderabadi biryani and dal tadka.
All the preparations were an absolute treat to our taste buds but what stole our hearts was the hospitality extended by Chetan.
Although we live in Abu Dhabi city, we still feel it worthwhile to drive all the way to CORIANDER in Al Ain again and again to get more and more surprises during every visit.
Our gastronomical journey with CORIANDER has just begun and we cannot wait till our next visit to explore more.
Dining at CORIANDER was indeed a delightful experience with generous portions, reasonable pricing, innovative creations and most importantly heart touching hospitality.
CORIANDER here we come again....

After work, my colleagues and I went out for a bite to eat. It was 5 o clock in the afternoon, and the dinner rush was not yet there. We were greeted friendly by the staff and shown a table. There were only one or two other tables occupied by people at the time, so we were quite secluded. The paper was put on the table, and the order was made seamlessly. The staff was creative and friendly, designing beautiful patterns with the sauce of the bucket. We were 3 ladies eating from the one bucket, and there was still some leftover rice when we finished. The rice portion is quite big , and I think if it were two males eating , they would easily finish all. The drinks that came with the meal were truly refreshing as we had the passionfruit and berry mojitos. They did take a bit long with clean up after we were done , but the vibe and music played by the staff made up for it. We had a blast and made amazing memories. I thoroughly enjoyed the experience and can't wait to bring my partner here to experience the humble hospitality and lovely food. Salamat po!!
Parking: The restaurant is situated on the corniche of Sharjah. Upon entering the service road, you enter a paid parking area. Parking is validated in store and easy to access.

column9:
Turkish cuisine, famously known for its kebabs and köfte, it is actually so much, much more!
Bosporus is a great spot for Turkish food!
Well worth a visit if you are looking for authentic Turkish and Mediterranean food.
We had a lovely lunch and everything was spot on. From the moment we walked in we felt very welcomed. Great hospitality and service!
Our food, especially my lahana sarma, mix dolma and salad all served together with Turkish bread-Simit (a circular bread, typically encrusted with sesame seeds or curekot / nigella sativa ) and no-knead bread (flat, fluffy traditional bread usually topped with sesame seeds, sometimes with pul biber, either way it’s just delicious!)
The attentive and friendly service by Murat and Noor was top notch!
Unfortunately they didn’t have my favourite sahlep but instead I’ve had creamy delicious sutli with pistachios along with the famous Turkish çay served in a tulip-shaped glass called ince belli!
Very nice authentic experience!

And the view over the Yas Bay Harbour does not detract either.

Rasoi Ghar Restaurant
I was in Yas Mall on the weekend and decided to get some food from
Rasoi Ghar Restaurant.
The restaurant is located on the ground floor just above Ferrari World.
I was warmly greeted by a very friendly gentleman. I opted for a Royal Meal Box. This is a thali in a takeaway. Everything comes neatly packed. There are 3 types, small, medium and large.
The Royal Meal Box comes with 2 starters. 4 main curries. 1 rice. 6 roti. 2 sweet desserts. Pickles and mouth freshener sauf.
Food was delicious.
This is a pure vegetarian restaurant.
Nice spacious dining area.
Friendly and polite staff.
Mall parking is available.
Wheelchair accessible.

Being Indian, I truly love desi food and anything desi. When I got to know that Rasoi Ghar, my favorite thali restaurant from Karama, Dubai has opened up here, I knew I had to pay a visit ASAP!
Same pricing, same delicious food, I literally felt like home.
Always and I mean it, ALWAYS visit Rasoi Ghar on an empty stomach or you're truly going to regret not eating it all. The variety is HUGE, that you have got to try a little bit of every dish, every drink, every dessert, and every accompaniment.
There is a new menu every single day, so you've never have the same meal again - and that is the best part of this concept. You always get a whole new thali to try with every visit.
Best not to divulge too much, as this place has got to surprise you!

Disappointing food at a very high price point. I was really excited to try the spot because of the great reviews. But both my friend and I felt the food was a huge miss. We ordered dahi puri, butter chicken, paneer tikka masala, chili cheese naans, and a mango lassi. Very standard and typical menu items to judge an Indian restaurant by. And we’re both not picky eaters. The mango lassi simply wasn’t good - my friend couldn’t drink it past two sips. It had a strange flavor which was neither sweet nor tangy. The dahi puri and complimentary papads were probably the best thing we had all night. Savory and well seasoned. The butter chicken had 3-4 pieces of chicken, and just didn’t taste like much. Same with the paneer tikka masala. They’re typically such flavorful dishes but the combination of seasoning and the preparation at India Palace just fell flat for us. They just did not taste great. The chili cheese naan was quite appetizing though - it was one of the only saving graces of the curry dishes. In the end, we paid almost 200 AED for food that missed the mark. There’s way better Indian food throughout the Dubai and Sharjah areas that you should opt for over this spot.

I had a wonderful experience at Chagh Kebab restaurant. The staff was friendly and attentive, the atmosphere was cozy and inviting, and the food was delicious and satisfying. I ordered the Adana Kebab and the Special Grill Mix, and I was not disappointed. The Adana Kebab was spicy and juicy, with a nice charred flavor. The Special Grill Mix had a variety of meats, such as lamb chops, chicken wings, beef skewers, and kofta. They were all tender and well-seasoned, and came with rice, salad, bread, and sauces. The portions were generous and filling. I also enjoyed the Aromatic laban, which was a refreshing yogurt drink with mint and cucumber. It was a perfect accompaniment to the spicy food. I would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone who loves authentic Turkish cuisine. It is one of the best places to eat in Abu Dhabi. Thank you, Chagh Kebab, for a memorable meal!
If you are looking for a taste of Turkish traditional food, you should definitely visit Chagh Kebab restaurant. It is a place where you can enjoy the rich and diverse flavors of Turkey, from the spicy and savory kebabs to the sweet and creamy baklava. You will feel like you are in Istanbul, with the warm and welcoming service, the colorful and cozy decor, and the aromatic and delicious food. Chagh Kebab restaurant is more than just a restaurant, it is a cultural experience. Don’t miss this opportunity to discover the wonders of Turkish cuisine.

My only critique is that the prices are on the high side, but for the quality of food and service that you receive, it is definitely worth it.
Black Salt is definitely worth trying, they just do not disappoint.

University city of Sharjah is emerging as a new eating hub, The Black Salt is one of the best restaurant among all.  It has a fancy yet simple interiors, done mostly in black, which gives it a very vintage & classy look. They serve awesome food & drinks with really fantastic presentation, which makes this place special. They also do a great fusions of authentic flavors with gastronomy. The staff is very nice & helpful.
Coming back on the food. We were invited there for the tasting session, so we tried a number of varieties there.
For Starters, we were served-
- Quinoa Tabouleh- a nice fusion of Arabic tabouleh salad with healthy quinoa.
- Fiery Bites- these were dynamite chicken bites. The sauce was very nice & not very spicy.
- Salmon tikka with ruffles- Nice combo of fish with chips.
- Mac n Cheese Nachos- It was crispy on the outside & nice & soft on the inside.
- Crispy chicken sliders.
- Wagyu sliders
For the Main Course-
- Shish Tawook on Paratha- It was a nice fusion of shish Tawook & Paratha .
- Butter Chicken Chow- Butter Chicken  served in a bun bowl.
- Pepper Chicken Pasta- this pasta was very nice and had a great pepper twist.
- Slow cooked Pulled beef served with garlic bread.
-
Now the most important part of any meal....Dessert-
- Red Velvet Cake- Red velvet cake served in the form of a  tower with 4 layers.
- Milk cake with white chocolate Dome- very artistic presentation & delicious in taste.
- Date cake served inside the caramel dome.
The Pretty drinks we had were-
- Peach iced Tea- The tea can not be more attractive than this one.
- Pinacolada- Yet another interestingly presented drink.
- Lemon & mint Mojito- As res fresh ingredients as it looks.
Overall a great place with great food with awesome presentation. Would love to go there again.

We went to Black Salt Restaurant because of a friend's recommendation. We were looking for a place close by to have dinner. The seating area is somewhat limited and it is an mostly open area; so no intimacy at all. Our host was quite nice and recommended some dishes but we ended up ordering the Chicken Fajita Messy Fries and the Citrus Corn on the Cob for starters. For the main, we ordered the Adana Kebab. Overall, it is a nice place but the chefs were noticeably loud especially at the table we were sitting at. I would definitely try it again.

Having never been to a Raclette Night till date, this was a new experience for me. With 3 glasses of wine and a raclette platter per person at AED. 189, I found that quite reasonable considering that most of the time, a glass of wine costs anything between AED. 40-60!
We choose to sit outdoors - to enjoy the lovely music as well as the weather. We started off with a glass of red wine from Chile. It wasn't a sweet wine, and that was a great choice as I had the server choose it for me.
Next, we were served with a molten raclette on sauteed ratte potatoes with beef chorizo on the side.
While the beef chorizo was super juicy and delicious, what made me love this dish was the perfectly cooked potatoes topped with cheese. The cheese literally melted into the potatoes cracks and it was the best basic potatoes I have ever eaten.
I could not wait longer for the platter of cold cuts and cheeses, so we requested for the same along with our second glass of wine, white wine this time.
The platter consisted of walnuts, prunes, figs, cold cuts of beef and chicken, along with a variety of cheese and crackers.
A fresh plate of bread was provided on the side.
If you're a vegetarian like my friend who joined me, you can still enjoy this platter as long as you have a companion who loves meat along with you!
The crackers with cheese and the beef cold cuts made for a delicious cracker!
Everything was great, and worth every dirham, for real!
As this offer does not provide any desserts, we went ahead with Valrhona Chocolate Pecan and Caramel Bar.
Filled with milk chocolate mouse, this dessert was a wonderful ending to the night.
column12: Jones The Grocer Al Muneera_Melissa Pinto_1

We will come back again with our circle of friends soon ✨

First time here - my husband has been going on about this place for months, but it isn't very cost effective. So I thought he would be thrilled to go here for his birthday.
Made reservations via WhatsApp - for the Medieval dinner for Two + drinks - 699AED. Gave our order atleast an hour in advance and accepting to push our reservations as we were running a bit late after work.
Now... First impressions, the location itself was a bit tricky to find, it was remote and dark. Once we found it we parked at the free parking space and went in.
It definitely embraces the Viking theme, the entrance has a small area adorned with intricately carved viking motifs.
Our host was Sergey, quirky/energetic. We were led to the main dining area, which was lit with a few dimmed chandeliers, wooden tables and benches, with faux stoles. Offcourse, the table itself was matching to the theme with dimly lit candles and a somewhat disproportionate dinner plate and utensils.
The ambiance was quite nice but I'm a little aversed to eating at a place where I can't really see my food, sensory stimulus aids to the experience after all.
Now the 5 course meal, enjoyable but lacked in certain consistencies.
The amuse-bouche was crunchy but a little bland. The meat salad was delish but the triquetra was a disappointment. French onion soup was lush. Now our main course, was a mix of all 5 dishes,
One piece of the chicken was dry and bland while the other was succulent.
My husband enjoyed the meats(ribeye/lamb). The salmon was dry/lacked flavor, but the oven-grilled eggplant was surprisingly delectable.
Finally the dessert, the apple pie knockoff dish, which was plated out to wish my husband (which I'm grateful for), the pastry was burned, but it was definitely more palatable then the cheesecake like, somewhat questionable option.
I won't question the quality of the produce itself, which I do believe meets standards, but the flavor profile was off putting.
Additionally, we had ordered the lava cheese bread (good cheese pull) and the moon pie(basically over fried potato wedges without any flavoring).
The drinks, they didn't have diet options for soft drinks so we chose the fruit drinks believing it to be freshly made - but no. The pineapple was alright but I do believe the orange juice was spoilt(had a strange metallic taste) - we asked for it to be changed immediately.
Our servers were pleasant, but seemed a little distracted.
My husband and I thoroughly enjoyed the performances.
The final bill with the service fee and tax , the Fazaa discount came to about 728 AED.
I must admit that I found the final bill to be a bit higher than expected for the Average joe ,but I wanted to treat my husband to an experience.
However, I believe that ensuring a balance between cost, customer service and value would enhance the overall appeal of this place.
Conclusively, a One - time must visit.

In our humble opinion, Coriander deserves 4.5⭐️
A bit about us first, so that you'll understand recommendations - prior to visiting Coriander, we were 2 very hungry individuals - one, who loves loves loves spicy food (as in - there's no such thing as too spicy) and one whose eyes start to water as soon as someone mentions the word spicy.
We ordered 5 spices salmon (appetiser), paneer tikka curry, aubergine (=eggplant) curry (b-something on the menu), pilau with veg and nuts, naan filled with mozzarella cheese and mango lassi.
Salmon was the best thing ever. It was slightly spicy (according to the person who is not the spicy eater), but still so so good. So if you ever come here  do try salmon. Also very good (5⭐️ items) were: paneer tikka curry (also slightly spicy, but not hot spicy, edible spicy, but you'll feel it a bit) and mango lassi. The rest of the dishes were about 4⭐️ (maybe 3.8). The aubergine curry was less spicy than paneer curry.
Oh, the complimentary drink shot was also very nice and served visually appealing.
Vegetarian options: Plenty vegetarian options available.
Parking: Located in a mall, so plenty of parking available (covered).

really small, cute place that’s a little hidden in muweilah road. although zushi has been around for a while, its only gained insane traction recently and we decided to give it a go.
atmosphere - it was a little stuffy in there, but it could’ve been because the restaurant was absolutely packed. the spotlights are quite annoying and bright, maybe not the best choice. could’ve opted for the small side lights that are used for the booth tables.
service - we arrived at 10:30 pm and had to wait for 10 minutes for a spot, which was fine since it was the third day of eid. person on the phone wasn’t the nicest when we called since they said they won’t serve us if there was no table available. honestly could’ve simply told us of the waiting time and that’s it.
food - for appetizers, we got the tataki (salmon), dynamite shrimp & kani salad. as for maki, we got bang bang, spicy tuna, tobiko, spicy beef & shrimp tempura.
for dessert, we got the chocolate volcano (honestly thought it needed more chocolate on top, cake layer was too dry).
i’d highly recommend the tataki, bang bang, tobiko and shrimp tempura. wasn’t too big on the spicy beef to be honest.
soft drink portions are really small, so i’d go for mocktails instead.
if you like to have wasabi and ginger with your sushi, make sure to ask them to bring it for you since they didn’t serve it with our dishes. only downside is that they don’t accept cash whatsoever - so bare that in mind!
definitely a place worth checking out, but nothing insanely special.

We chose this eatery as we were passing by. My family was seated in the curtained booths and the restaurant was oozing a great Indian atmosphere. We ordered two whole tandoori chickens, a gosht biriyani, a butter chicken biriyani and a plethora of little nibbles. To break our fast, they provided Laban and a small fruit selection containing grapes, melons, dates and nuts. Beginning with the tandoori chickens, they came on a naan bread bed. The chicken had a slight spicy kick to it that elevated it from boring to elite level. Most importantly, my kids rated it 10/10. The butter chicken biryani was delicious. It arrived on a large plate served with a pot of butter chicken sauce on the side. There were plenty of chicken tikka pieces and the whole combination was top notch. My wife had the gosht biryani, which was served in a sealed pot. The mutton was cooked to perfection and the flavour was outstanding. My son said the naan bread were some of the best he’s had and took some extra ones with him. The staff were absolutely fantastic, they delivered a perfect service that we felt obliged to mention our satisfaction to the Manager. I would highly recommend this restaurant highly to anyone looking for delicious Indian food.
Kid-friendliness: The staff were very friendly to our children and seated us away from the busy parts

India Palace restaurant at Rak Mall has an impeccable reputation for its delicious food and professional service. I had the pleasure of dining at the restaurant and was extremely impressed with every aspect of the experience.
Firstly, the food was exceptional. Each dish was expertly prepared with fresh, high-quality ingredients, and the flavors were perfectly balanced. The menu offered a great variety of classic Indian dishes and contemporary twists that catered to all tastes. I particularly loved the chicken jalfrezy  which were packed full of flavor and spice.
The service was equally impressive. From the moment I entered the restaurant, the staff was welcoming and attentive. Our waiter was well-informed about the menu and offered helpful suggestions throughout our meal. The staff was quick to refill our water and drinks and made sure that we were comfortable and satisfied throughout.
The ambiance of the restaurant was also noteworthy. The decor was elegant and tasteful, providing a comfortable and cozy feeling while dining. The lighting contributed and enhanced my overall dining experience.
Overall, I had a fantastic dining experience at India Palace restaurant. The food, service, and ambiance were all exceptional, and I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for an authentic Indian dining experience. I look forward to dining here again in the future.

One of the upcoming & embryonic food streets or dining hub of UAE resides in the University City of Sharjah and Black Salt is probably one of the best restaurants among them.
Black Salt is a place crowded by youth because of their authentic fusion food, vintage and classy ambience and good dining experience all together.
Their staff is very friendly, helpful and demonstrate positive vibes due to the fact that this place has a very unique strategy of diversification, where they have 30 people with 13 different nationalities and 5 different religions.
This is one of our favourite dinning places in Sharjah and being called for a food tasting session there was a dream come true for us.
Overall an amazing experience with great fusion food, amazing service & classy ambience.
Foodie rahgeer will definitely give them a 5-foodie star.

Deccan Delight is great for families and bachelors alike. Comfortable seating and a pleasant ambience was very welcoming. The staff was hospitable and quite accommodating.

If you aren't a fan of spicy preparation, please inform them while ordering as Deccan dishes can be heavy on the chillies. We enjoyed the spices though.
We will definitely return to try more of their preparations.

A home away from home for some authentic lip-smacking Hyderabadi delicacies!
We were invited for dinner in Ajman to try the food Deccan Delight had to offer and believe us when we say every minute spent on the journey was worth every morsel of food we had at this place!
Located in Al Rashidiya 2, Ajman, this place was a bit of a drive for us, but the travel seems trivial in comparison to the rich and flavorful food served here. The restaurant itself is quite spacious, perfect for a large gathering of friends or family. The walls are adorned with tidbits of historical facts about the cuisine served here.
Most of the dishes here are made using traditional methods which truly reflects in the food flavor as well as texture wise. All the spices used are authentic Hyderabadi spice mixes which is the reason why each bite was an explosion of flavors in our mouth.
The place has a homely and warm atmosphere with musical hits from Coke Studio playing to make the dining experience even more pleasant. Last but not the least of the positives about this place is the staff. Hospitality here is top notch, the servers are humble and attentive and not to forget the owner Mr. Ali at the front of the house and the culinary genius Ms. Rida Mirza managing the show behind the scenes.
Deccan Delight Special: A welcome drink that had chunks of watermelon infused with rose water and sabza seeds. It was slightly on the sweeter side but a refreshing glass right after work!
Lemonade [AED 5]: Freshly squeezed lemon juice with the right balance of sweetness. The strawberries added to the mix makes it for a good detox drink as well. A good palate cleanser.
Shahi Haleem [AED 16]: We were a bit skeptical to try this because we were not fans of haleem to begin with but the haleem served here has taken us to the Haleem side! It is made without the use of any fancy gadgets but by hand which makes a world of a difference. You’ll have to taste it to believe it. Aromatic and rich and full of flavour, this meaty dish is a MUST at Deccan Delight.
Patthar Ka Gosht [AED 21]: We are sure all the MEAT eaters will fall in love with the dish. A Hyderabad special starter that is cooked on a slab of mountain stone. The marination takes two hours to get all those delicious flavors on point. Thin slices of lamb tossed with pepper, papaya and yoghurt are then grilled on the Deccan stone. The meat was tender and juicy served along with the mint dip that took the whole dish to another level. It had the perfect spice level and too good that we could have just the meat as a whole meal. DO NOT LEAVE WITHOUT TRYING IT! Thank us later, once you’re in love with it too.
Fiery Chicken 65 [AED 16]: Sizzle, sizzle…. The chicken is served on a sizzler loaded with the spicy sauce and garnished with curry leaves. It was well cooked and just glided through our spoons. You don’t need no knife to crack this one.
Dum ka Murg [AED 15]: A rich and nutty gravy loaded with chunks of juicy chicken. The taste was simply fabulous and the secret behind that is the spices are brought from Hyderabad to maintain the authentic taste.
Shahi Gosht: This dish was newly introduced and is yet to come on the menu. For us we definitely would love to come back for more of it. The mutton was cooked so well and wrapped in a thick marinade of mint which made great difference to the flavor. This was another one of our favorites that we would love to come back for at Deccan Delight.
Kacche Gosht Ki Dum Biryani [AED 18]: Pieces of lamb that are succulent as ever paired with an aromatic and perfectly cooked basmati rice is what you get with this biryani! The meat has that fall-off-the-bone tenderness which is what we look for in a good biryani. I’ve already discredited all the ‘Hyderabadi Biryanis’ I’ve had elsewhere in the past because the one served here is the real deal.
The staff here are on their A game!
Ofcourse we are coming back! We’ve already marked our calendars for our next trip to a little piece of Hyderabad in Ajman.

Fiery Chicken 65 [AED 16]: Sizzle, sizzle…. The chicken is served on a sizzler loaded with the spicy sauce and garnished with curry leaves. It was well cooked and just glided through our spoons. You don’t need no knife to crack this one.
Dum ka Murg [AED 15]: A rich and nutty gravy loaded with chunks of juicy chicken. The taste was simply fabulous and the secret behind that is the spices are brought from Hyderabad to maintain the authentic taste.
Shahi Gosht: This dish was newly introduced and is yet to come on the menu. For us we definitely would love to come back for more of it. The mutton was cooked so well and wrapped in a thick marinade of mint which made great difference to the flavor. This was another one of our favorites that we would love to come back for at Deccan Delight.
Kacche Gosht Ki Dum Biryani [AED 18]: Pieces of lamb that are succulent as ever paired with an aromatic and perfectly cooked basmati rice is what you get with this biryani! The meat has that fall-off-the-bone tenderness which is what we look for in a good biryani. I’ve already discredited all the ‘Hyderabadi Biryanis’ I’ve had elsewhere in the past because the one served here is the real deal.
The staff here are on their A game!
Ofcourse we are coming back! We’ve already marked our calendars for our next trip to a little piece of Hyderabad in Ajman.

column9:
Its our first time, and one of our rajasthani friend brought us here.We visited their restaurant to try *Their THALI* with other few friends. Their staff are on eof the biggest asset of the company, very humble and hospitable. GOPI , SHEILA, AND one more indian server ( i couldn't remember his name). They made our whole experience here outstanding, and we would like to be served by them again in the future.
The area is not so crowded,  parking available

column3: Rajasthan Al Malaki - Restaurant مطعم راجستان الملكي
column9:
Sometimes you eat out; sometimes you have a dining experience! This is the latter. Although it is Indian food, the cuisine is different than what you might think. Even dishes with the same name (e.g. palek paneer) are flavored uniquely. And by unique, I also mean tasty!! Sweet. Savory, spicey. Mild. Everything. And at 40 AED a person for everything, it's a noteworthy deal!
The service was incredible too, including detailed stories about the food and its uses in Rajastanian culture (see video I posted). Plus, it's an all you can eat scenario! They insist on keeping your little bowls of food filled. I almost couldn't walk out. Too full.
The location is in classic dusty, wild, non-fancy Sharjah. In my opinion, this only adds to the global feel of the experience.
This place earns Dr. Matt's stamp of approval!
Vegetarian options: It's all vegetarian
Kid-friendliness: They are welcoming of kids! Big time

You’re slowly biting into a piece of Sambousek covered in Hummus, with some Hindbeh leaves in the mix… You close your eyes to savor the moment as you let the explosion of flavors invade you. A nostalgic Fairuz song is playing in the background, and a soft breeze is caressing your cheeks. Life is good. It’s especially good at Em Sherif where the culinary experience combines richness and delicateness, comfort and elegance, past and present.
A word of caution: you may have to roll out of the place, as walking would be physically impossible after what can only be described as a gargantuan feast… So you may want to pace yourself. It’s a set menu that takes the stress out of ordering, and ensures that energy is re-directed towards devouring the meal. And it’s classically Lebanese, with the cold and hot appetizers, the warm main dishes, and the desserts, all with small refined portions.
Everything was delicious but if I were to pick some highlights:
- The minced meat Rkakat and Sambousek were so scrumptious yet delicate at the same time
- The Kibbeh with yogurt is another hit. The flavoring, the umami, the freshness of the yoghurt…combine magically together
- Then when you think you’re done… comes a pleasant surprise: A muffin-shaped puff pastry filled with rice, minced meat, chicken and a whole array of condiments (raisins, almonds, shaved carrots, peas), sprinkled with a cinnamon flavored gravy… Sort of a “Riz aa Djej” with a twist. You won’t know what hit you. And you might come back for a second, third, maybe even a fourth serving.
- The desserts.. what a beautiful note to end this extraordinary performance on. The date and molasses cake might trigger a few inappropriate sounds of approval. The Mhallabye with the loukoum and biscuits will feel decadently sinful.
It’s a beautiful experience. Yes your tummy will beg you to stop, but your your heart and soul will beg for an Encore…

Our first time at Steak Bar Sushi was nice. The place looks great and has a cool, fancy feel with good music. The food was okay in quality but the portions were small and the taste was just average.
We started with the Raunchy Mushroom, which was okay but not great, so I'd give it a 3 out of 5. We also tried six skewers, which were better, earning a 4 out of 5. The five sushi sets we had were alright, scoring 3 out of 5, with the Crazy Salmon being the best of them.
The ribs we ordered weren't good – the taste, quality, and amount were all disappointing, so 2 out of 5 for them. The Bife de Ancho steak was much better, with a tasty sauce, getting a 4 out of 5 from us. We also had two sides of Messy Potato, which were good and get a 4 out of 5.
We each had a glass of wine to drink. For dessert, we chose the Chocolate Orgasm and Caramelized Pineapple, which were good, scoring 4/5 and 3/5.
In total, six of us ate and the bill was about $200. Overall, the place is nice to look at and the food is alright, However it's over rated and expensive for what you get, especially because the portions aren't big.

column3: Rajasthan Al Malaki - Restaurant مطعم راجستان الملكي
column9:
The restaurant is mid-sized, we felt it was a bit cramped. The tables were adorned with Rajasthani art work and the walls were filled with Rajasthani paintings. Rajasthan Al Malaki offers vegetarian food, special shout-out to their Thali. On weekends they have special thali- Royal Thali.  Thalis are served with Chaas or Flavored Indian buttermilk. We also had their special Lassi. It was delicious, thick, sweet and creamy, which was not part of the thali though…
We were served 2 types of starters, Kaddi and Rice, 4 types of vegetables, 3 types of Roti, 2 types of sweets and popular Rajasthani dishes like Dal Baati Churma, Gatte Ki Sabji, Pachkuute Ka Saag  and Dahi Vada and everything was lip smacking.
Only kacha parking spots available, since it was our first visit to this restaurant we found it quite challenging to arrive here even after pinning the location on Google map, as on all sides the road construction was in progress.
Regular Rajasthani Thali- Sunday to Thursday : 25 Dhs per person
Weekend(Royal) Rajasthani Thali- Friday & Saturday: 30 Dhs per person
Kids under 8- Half Price
Location- Behind DPS Sharjah Primary School, Muwailih Commercial, Sharjah
column12: Rajasthan Al Malaki - Restaurant مطعم راجستان الملكي_Mommy Traveller_1

If you are looking for perfection... Then this place should be your one and olny destination
It was the greatest experience i have ever had
*Let's start with the place! Everything is perfectly designed and managed. The helped is choosing the best table in the restaurant under a red tree next the window with a nice view! Nothing more to say, simply perfect! Chairs are very comfortable, lighting and music fit the place! Very nice bar in the middle!
*Regarding the food, the taste kept us speechless, mouthwatering plats and big portions perfectly presented! As appetizers we ordered ham and cheese surprise and salmon sensation sushi, 2 main dishes:the flaming "filet gourmet" and luscious veal and 2 glasses of wine! The dessert was on the house!
*Talking about perfection, we must not forget the staff! Highly professional and friendly staff(hostess and waiters ), smiling and checking tables all the time, you'll love how fast they will serve you and the way of doing it!
You'll know the essence of this professionalism, sociability and friendliness once you meet the owner Mr Charbel Makhlouf, he'll certainly visit your table, present himself, advice you what to order with the best description ever!

Yes, it was all the hype about Em Sherif and their high review scores that eventually aroused my curiosity. We were in the mood for Lebanese cuisine, so we decided to finally give it a try. When you go in, you notice that the restaurant is fancy, with its mirrored tables and silver cutlery (although I liked some aspects of the interior decoration more than others). A noteworthy issue to mention here is that the service was great from when we entered Em Sherif till when we left. The waiters were very welcoming and friendly, and swiftly brought the food to our table. Things work differently at Em Sherif; when you sit down you do not get a menu to choose from but instead the food directly starts coming your way. For a first-timer, the set menu descending at a fast pace in front of you as well as the waiters passing by with trays of food can be exciting, yet a bit overwhelming as you are trying to keep track of what is being offered and trying to taste everything. However, we did request for room to breathe when we were asked if we would like the hot constituents to be served. I am glad we did that because it was then that I enjoyed all the delicious flavors. Em Sherif does have great food. Their hummus is creamy and their humble labne is really really really good. From the items on the “hovering mezza” tray, the la7em bi3ajeen and sambousik were very tasty, and honestly I would rather that the tray land on the table permanently. The chickpeas in the balila were cooked perfectly and it was well seasoned, though a tad oily. I was surprised at how good the harak osbao was; it had the right amount of tanginess. Additionally, the marination of the skewered shrimps was great and I enjoyed the tender meat chunks (I preferred them to the chich taouk). I could go and on about the immense number of platters we tasted, but if I wanted to describe Em Sherif’s food concisely, it would be well-balanced; their seasoning and the combination of flavors were spot on. I also have to commend them on the kibbe nayye, which had the mint and onions within the mixture, meaning all you had to do was add the olive oil. After this feast of salted dishes, it was time for the sweet ones. Their um ali sauce is to die for! I loved their take on the foret noire presentation; it was placed in a bowl and the chocolate cake was in itself a moist hollow vessel in which the fruits and cream were placed. It seems the maamoul bi jibne is popping up everywhere nowadays, and I am a fan of it in general, and a fan of it at Em Sherif. The waiter places it on your plate and professionally slits it open so that the drizzle of syrup reaches the melted cheese beneath the crumbly crust. All in all, Em Sherif provides a rich set menu with a bit of everything and it left us feeling stuffed for the rest of the day.

Ginger and Co presents a nice dining experience that balances a casual atmosphere with a touch of sophistication, making it suitable for both everyday meals and special occasions. I went there after work based on a friend’s recommendation and it didn’t disappoint. Nestled in a quiet area, its terrace offered a secluded getaway that remained breezy even during the midsummer heat (July), which provided us with an ideal setting for a relaxed lunch.
The service at Ginger and Co is friendly, adding to the warm and welcoming ambiance of the place. The staff are attentive and ready to offer recommendations from their diverse menu, which is delightful for any sushi/ Japanese cuisine lover. The menu's richness extends beyond sushi to include a variety of hot noodle dishes, poke bowls, rice dishes, several options for appetizers, and weekly specials that cater to a range of tastes and dietary preferences (including several vegetarian options).
We got sushi, tamaki, and shrimp dumplings - each serving was prepared fresh, presented beautifully and promptly.
This establishment is particularly great for relaxed meals with friends and colleagues, offering a casual yet elevated environment that's also perfectly suited for a date or celebrating a special occasion. With its combination of good food, serene location, and courteous service, Ginger and Co stands out as a must-visit spot for both locals and visitors in the Hazmieh area.
Vegetarian options: Vegetable sushi - salads - vegetable noodles
Kid-friendliness: Welcoming environment

column9:
What a great surprise eating at Thunder Road Pizza was during our recent trip to the Ras Al Khamiah area.  Previously, we had attempted to road delivery from this restaurant but were too far out of their delivery area.
On this trip we ended up being only a few minutes away and instead of ordering delivery we would just check the place out in person.  Once arriving we were glad we did!  The inside is bright and airing with so much to absorb.  Route 66, motorcycle, 50's, paraphenalia and memorabilia decorate the walls and tables making this restaurant feel like a 50's cross between a ice cream stand and hamburger joint.  There is even a classic mint-conditioned Harley in the dining area.  All the staff were very happy and friendly and were quick to take care of us upon entering.
The menu has something for everyone - Italian favorites like pizza and calzones, to hamburgers and steaks, all types of salads, and side dishes to jont your other choices.  Make sure to leave room for Grandma's Apple Pie!  For our meal we had the Parmigiana Starter, the Calzone, and two burgers, the Road Burger and the Smoky Thunder.   All items were served quickly and piping hot.  The fries were perfect!  The only item which was lacking was the Calzone.  It was under-cooked and still quite doughy.  Everything else was spot on.  We look forward to our next trip to RAK and another night out at Thunder Road Pizza & Grill.
column12: Thunder Road Italian Restaurant-Al Riffah_Robert Kraeuter_1

When it comes to traditional fish cuisine, Babel Bahr stands out as a true gem in Lebanon. The restaurant excels in every aspect, offering a unique dining experience that sets it apart from typical seafood establishments.
One of the standout features of Babel Bahr is their authentic charcoal-grilled fish, a method that truly caters to the discerning palate of gourmet enthusiasts. Unlike the common gas or electric grilling methods, the use of real charcoal imparts a distinctive flavor and aroma to the fish that elevates the dining experience.
For an authentic taste of the region, I highly recommend trying the local fish varieties such as Ajaj, Braq, or Gazaleh, which are seasonal delights typically available until late summer. These fresh catches truly showcase the rich flavors of Lebanese seafood.
To complement your grilled fish, be sure to pair it with a glass of their excellent local Arak. The combination of grilled fish and Arak creates a harmonious blend of flavors that is sure to delight your taste buds.
Overall, Babel Bahr offers a culinary experience that is not to be missed for seafood aficionados looking to savor the best of Lebanese fish cuisine. From the charcoal-grilled delicacies to the superb local drinks, a visit to Babel Bahr promises a memorable dining experience.
Cheers

From the serene village in Bkaakafra, to the busy streets of London, passing by the large green landscape in Scotland off to Kyoto's imperial castles and Buddhist temples and Uruguay's wild life; a Star War's fan landed back on the 3rd floor of Maison M in Naccache.
Charbel Makhlouf, the new blood soaking in all the experience from his grandfather to marry it with his own as well as his studies in Management and Consumer behavior to transform it into a new concept and approach to the Japanese - American cuisine and educate our palates to accept and enjoy it!
Steakbarshushi: as simple as you can imagine, the name reflects what the outlet is serving: Steak, Sushi and a bar to mingle and enjoy a drink.
Knowing me, I used to be skeptical when a restaurant claims serving sushi and something else, but boy I was wrong!
Be ready to surrender to the experience, you even sign a paper to do that! When the elevator door opens, leave all you presumptions behind and you will not regret it.
A serene environment that surprisingly mixes even the steak and sushi atmosphere in the decoration and in a very subtle way.
Think wooden tables roughly cut each in a unique shape, homey feeling of different rustic chairs and cutlery, a green wall with a zen mood near a Japanese inspired seating, a rough rustic wooden bar, and cherry on the cake, homegrown peppers and basil among other aromatic plants and edible flowers.
A smooth lighting adds to the warmth of the place, and the music compliments the ambiance perfectly.
Now that your eyes and your mind are set free, comes the turn of the palate.
I was lucky to share my meal with Charbel, who introduced me to every item of the menu we tasted; grateful as ever I signed the paper and the journey started.
Raunchy mushrooms: homegrown Portobello soaking in miso herb dressing, rosemary, lemon zest, salt and black pepper: earthy flavors, I loved it
Yakitoris gently decorated with edible flowers and drizzled each with their marinating sauce:
Cheezy salmon: salmon stuffed with brie and bresaola grilled with eggplants: how balanced the mix was not to masque the taste of salmon, Chef you are a genius!
Beef chili and beef miso: with slices of mushrooms in the latter: as if the meat was not juicy enough to add those mouth-watering sauces and the flavors bursting in your mouth
Crispy onion jalapenos: house smoked salmon topped with buffalo mozzarella and covered with crispy onions, jalapeno and a Japanese spicy sauce to fire those palates with every bite.
Tuna salmon explosion: with a Japanese cucumber and trust me you will notice the difference and again to cherish that miso homemade sauce that is just enhancing every flavor
Spicy crab: yes the king crab meat, all dense, mixed with crispy wasabi and a side of flaming hot grilled green pepper
Othamleyeh shrimp: with every bite you will taste distinct flavors in euphoric way: pineapples, rice, shrimps, othamaleyi and teryaki sauce: who thought this tiny wrap can be that powerful
King salad: king crab over a bed of purslane, Mexican avocados and a light dressing
And now things got serious, the show went on with the steak, just to note that Charbel picks the veal and pampers them in his farm, where also many of the produce he uses are grown.
We tasted:
Luscious veal: served by Charbel himself where he cuts the cutlets and drizzles them with a light herby sauce, permission slip to eat using your hands!
Filet gourmet: also comes with a show! flaming the pieces to tickle the palate! A béarnaise sauce on the side to compliment the flavors.
Mac 'N' cheese for the baby in you! with a touch of truffle oil.
La finale signed by the virgin! Four layers of génoise, topped with praliné, dark chocolate and white cheese and chocolate infused with coconut and mint topped with a crunchy chocolate piece and served with a side of mint foam and three pieces of dark chocolate and dried fruits and nuts. Can not think of a better note to end this journey.

Lori's Restaurant in Lebanon stands as a culinary beacon, offering an exquisite dining experience that masterfully blends traditional Lebanese flavors with contemporary cooking techniques. Located in the heart of Lebanon, this restaurant boasts a charming atmosphere that immediately makes guests feel welcomed and valued.
The moment you step into Lori's, you are greeted by an elegantly decorated space that combines rustic charm with modern elegance. The decor, with its soothing colors and tasteful Lebanese accents, sets the stage for a memorable meal. The ambiance is enhanced by soft, ambient music that complements the dining experience without overpowering conversation.
The menu at Lori's is a testament to the rich culinary heritage of Lebanon. It features an array of dishes that celebrate the diversity and richness of Lebanese cuisine, from succulent grilled meats to vibrant, freshly prepared salads. Each dish is crafted using only the freshest local ingredients, ensuring that every bite conveys the authentic flavors of Lebanon. Been meaning to pass by Uptown Beirut for a while, and finally got the chance last night!
You just cant miss this place if you are passing by from outside, with all the beautiful lighting and colors.
As soon as you enter, you get thrown back to the 1950's with the vintage decoration, from walls, tables, chairs, all down to the very last details.
We sat on the upper terrace, as we were warmly welcomed by staff. We ordered fattouch, itch (a bit dry), hommus, labne with toum, mkanek, ras asfour, mhammara, and grilled farrouj.
All items were delicious, especially the mhammara!
Service was excellent, and all staff - waiters, hostesses, and managers - are extremely respectful.
Thank you Uptown Beirut for always keeping high standards. Definitely visiting again!

Uptown Beirut, located in Dbayeh, Lebanon, is a vibrant and bustling restaurant that offers a diverse menu featuring a wide range of dishes from various cuisines. As you enter the restaurant, you are greeted with a warm and welcoming ambiance, coupled with friendly staff ready to assist you throughout your dining experience.
The menu at Uptown Beirut is extensive, catering to different tastes and preferences. Starting with the salad section, the Grilled Halloumi Salad stands out as a delightful combination of fresh iceberg lettuce, rocca, cherry tomatoes, black olives, and balsamic dressing, topped with perfectly grilled halloumi cheese and pesto sauce. The flavors and textures blend harmoniously, creating a refreshing and satisfying salad.
For those seeking a unique flavor experience, the Chicken Avocado Sandwich is a must-try. The tender chicken breast marinated in flavorful spices is perfectly complemented by the richness of avocado. Served on a sandwich white bread with garlic mayo sauce, fresh iceberg lettuce, and a side of crispy French fries, this sandwich is a delightful combination of flavors and textures.
If you're in the mood for pasta, Uptown Beirut offers a range of options. The Pasta Al Pesto is a classic choice, featuring al dente pasta tossed in a fragrant pesto sauce, enhanced with fresh cream and grated Parmesan cheese. The dish is beautifully balanced, allowing the vibrant flavors of the basil and garlic to shine through.
Uptown Beirut also excels in its grills section. The Chich Tawouk, marinated chicken skewers, is a popular choice among diners. The juicy and tender chicken is grilled to perfection, accompanied by fresh tomatoes, onions, and Arabic bread. The dish is elevated by the aromatic garlic paste and chili bread, adding a delightful kick to each bite.
The dessert selection at Uptown Beirut is equally impressive. The Molten Cake is a chocolate lover's dream. The warm, gooey chocolate center is encased in a moist and decadent cake, creating a delightful contrast of textures. Each bite is a heavenly experience that leaves you craving for more.
To complement the dining experience, Uptown Beirut offers a wide range of beverages, including refreshing fresh juices, soft drinks, and a selection of hot beverages like Lebanese coffee and cappuccino. The service at Uptown Beirut is attentive and efficient, ensuring that your needs are met promptly and with a smile.
In summary, Uptown Beirut in Dbayeh is a fantastic dining destination that offers a diverse menu, delicious flavors, and a welcoming ambiance. Whether you're in the mood for a refreshing salad, a satisfying sandwich, a comforting pasta dish, or a mouthwatering grilled meal, Uptown Beirut has something to satisfy every craving. With its attentive service and a wide range of beverage options, Uptown Beirut provides a memorable dining experience that will leave you wanting to come back for more.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Sapori E Vini and it left me completely awestruck with its exceptional service and incredible team of waiters. From the moment I stepped through the doors, I knew I was in for an extraordinary dining experience.
Upon entering, I was warmly greeted. The staff's attentiveness was unparalleled as they swiftly guided me to my table, ensuring my comfort throughout the evening. It was evident that every member of the team was dedicated to providing a flawless dining experience.
The waiters were not only knowledgeable about the extensive menu but also passionate about the culinary delights they served. They graciously took the time to explain each dish, offering recommendations based on personal preferences. Their attention to detail and willingness to cater to individual dietary requirements was truly commendable.
Now, let's talk about the food. The menu boasted a tantalizing array of traditional Italian dishes that captured the essence of Italy's rich culinary heritage. Each plate was a work of art, meticulously crafted with fresh, high-quality ingredients. Every bite was a burst of flavor that transported me to the streets of Rome or the coastal towns of Sicily.
One dish that particularly stood out was the goat cheese pizza.
The service at this Italian gem was flawlessly synchronized, with the waiters seamlessly attending to every need without being intrusive. I personally had Chiara and Dahami I think were the names of my servers, extremely pleasant people with a lot of passion which was really evident to see.
Empty plates were promptly cleared, and glasses were attentively refilled. The wait staff's genuine smiles and warm personalities created an inviting atmosphere, making me feel like an honored guest throughout the entire evening.
The restaurant itself was tastefully decorated, exuding an ambiance that was both elegant and cozy.
In conclusion, my experience at this Italian restaurant was truly exceptional. From the impeccable service to the delectable cuisine, every aspect exceeded my expectations. I highly recommend visiting this establishment to anyone seeking an unforgettable dining experience. Prepare to be transported to Italy with every bite and indulge in the finest hospitality Lebanon has to offer.

There are no grilled meats on the menu, just a lot of appetizers and seafood dishes. You can select a fish and have it cooked in a seemingly infinite number of ways, the waiting staff is that accommodating. The desserts are almost out of this world in terms of presentation, content and taste.  A high-end restaurant with prices to match but well worth it.

column9:
Situated on the ground floor at the rear of the Etihad Airways Centre building and in close proximity to the Al Maneera residential complex, this outlet features all the good things you expect from a Jones the grocer cafe/restaurant
In particular this location also has a liquor licence so they can serve wine and alcoholic beverages with meals. The causal dining atmosphere and quality meals makes it an ideal place to entertain guests.
The food at JTG never disappoints and is always fresh and tasty. The menu changes every few months so you won't get bored with the same selections.
As typical for this chain, the price is on the expensive side so it's not the place you would dine daily but if you are looking for a tasty meal or a place to impress a guest or a date, then JTG would be ideal.
On the negative side, there is no public parking anywhere nearby so unless you taxi in, walk in, work in the ETIHAD office or live in the Al Maneera complex, then this is a real problem. Perhaps the JTG at the nearby Al Raha gardens plaza would be more convenient.
The free Wi-Fi requires Facebook, Twitter or Instagram login or alternatively you can log in using your email address BUT this information is given to third parties for the purposes of telemarketing. So effectively this is not free Wi-Fi and in fact could open you up to a deluge of spam.

As typical for this chain, the price is on the expensive side so it's not the place you would dine daily but if you are looking for a tasty meal or a place to impress a guest or a date, then JTG would be ideal.
On the negative side, there is no public parking anywhere nearby so unless you taxi in, walk in, work in the ETIHAD office or live in the Al Maneera complex, then this is a real problem. Perhaps the JTG at the nearby Al Raha gardens plaza would be more convenient.
The free Wi-Fi requires Facebook, Twitter or Instagram login or alternatively you can log in using your email address BUT this information is given to third parties for the purposes of telemarketing. So effectively this is not free Wi-Fi and in fact could open you up to a deluge of spam.

Society Bistro stands out as a delightful dining spot known for its appealing ambiance and delicious meals, all at remarkably low prices. The restaurant is typically full, making it essential to book in advance or be prepared to wait for a table. Although the service can sometimes seem distracted due to the crowd, the overall atmosphere remains charming, romantic, and somewhat elegant. It's notably impressive how the bistro manages to offer food of such quality at a fraction of the cost compared to similar bistros.
Recently, there's been a slight dip in quality, yet the offerings remain good. Our meal included a quinoa Scamorza salad, which was generous though lacking in originality. The poulet au citron was excellent, but you can barely taste the lemon. The truffle burger and fondant au chocolat were enjoyable, yet neither dish stood out as exceptional.
I endorse this restaurant for its excellent cuisine, charming French atmosphere, and unbeatable prices.

column9: We loved this steak house, and this was the first we liked in Lebanon. Casual and trendy.  Great idea for a specialty grill with four main dish items on the menu. With fries or baked potato, Lulu lettuce salad, butter/herb sauce for steak, which service advised was good also for baked potato.  It wasn't. We ordered daily special rib eye for 2 for more than twice the cost of a single dish  but wasn't enough for two. But very tasty Columbian beef rather than Brazil beef. Looked more like an awesome prime rib steak, which Londoners serve with Yorkshire Pudding. Here's an idea for this restaurant. Want free recipe? French fries with steak? Come on! And fries were less than ordinary. The baked potato was also mediocre - more boiled than baked. Butter with herbs was a fail for us. Try butter alone, or with little garlic. Or just get some sour cream and toast the potatoes well for five stars. Our steak had a rib bone with stringy meat near the bone that was raw since near the bone, but that was the nature of this steak, except the second person had a smaller share. Nevertheless, we loved the place and the food. Our critique points are hopeful suggestions so we can make this place a regular. Also, should have mustard options - English hot mustard from powder, Dijon variety, BBQ or other easy off the shelf condiments or sauces. Loved the experience enough to comment.

Ok, the decor really needs to be recognized; hence the separate gallery. I love the interior. I love the planted trees bringing the garden indoors. I love the touch of gravel that is placed on a section of the floor in front of the wine bottles; when feet step on it, a pleasant sounding crunch tickles your ears. The hanging pots and pans, the fresh fruits and vegetables on display, the warm red bricks, and the wooden tables and chairs; they all complement each other and the attention to detail is amazing. Another lovely area to sit in is actually the real outdoors where a pergola stands on the green grass overlooking the terrace. If it had not been so hot, I would have opted to sit there. I should mention that there is an additional element for the children outside; a small form of playground that they can enjoy. All in all, one really needs to appreciate the effort that has been put to create a beautiful environment to sit and have a meal in.
Now let’s get to the food prepared by Italian chef Ignazio from Tuscany. First, they placed a dainty compilation of breads on the table. They looked really rustic and pretty, being meticulously arranged in brown paper. After scrutinizing the menu, we ordered the marinated tuna carpaccio which was good. For salads, we had the chicken quinoa salad and the shrimp salad. I really liked the chicken quinoa salad, but the item I liked the most was the pizza. Baked in a wood-fired oven, the pizza crust was delicious. I usually prefer to eat the tasty insides of a pizza, as opposed to the crust; but with this one, I had to have the crust too. The tomato sauce was a flavorful base for the toppings to be scattered on. I would definitely order the pizza again. The tagliata had delicious flavors too, but the meat had a sort of tough exterior that takes away from the taste of the juicy inside. As for the shrimp pasta dish, the sauce was too fishy for my liking, but that is a matter of preference. They then offered us ice cream on the house; it was homemade gelato which deserves respect. Another homemade item on the dessert menu was the chocolate fondant infused with raspberry. The cake holding the chocolate sauce tasted amazing. However, the savor of the raspberry was muted and did not seep through with the overpowering flow of chocolate. On an ending note, I have to add that the service was great, and I would visit this restaurant again.

Dar al Amar is in the heart of Tripoli at Dam w Farez street. From the moment you step inside, you are greeted with warm hospitality and a cozy ambiance that sets the tone for a delightful dining experience. The restaurant's Lebanese cuisine is a true reflection of traditional flavors and authenticity.
The menu at Dar al Amar offers a wide variety of Lebanese dishes, from mouthwatering mezzes to hearty mains and delectable desserts. Each dish is prepared with care and attention to detail, showcasing the rich culinary heritage of Lebanon.
In addition to the delicious food, the service at Dar al Amar is top-notch. The staff is friendly, attentive, and knowledgeable about the menu, making recommendations based on your preferences. The overall dining experience is enhanced by the welcoming atmosphere and the genuine care shown by the team.
Overall, Dar al Amar is a must-visit Lebanese restaurant in Tripoli, North Lebanon. Whether you are a local resident or a visitor to the area, this restaurant offers a culinary journey that celebrates the essence of Lebanese cuisine. I highly recommend Dar al Amar for a memorable dining experience that will leave you
