Of all the things I was excited to eat in Lebanon, fresh seafood was high on my list. Following a visit to Jbeil, my family and I decided to try out Babel Bahr, excited both by its excellent reputation and setting right by the water.
When we arrived at Babel, the restaurant was relatively empty, although I chalk this down mostly to our time of arrival, as 6pm is not quite lunch or dinner. The space itself is impressive, with the entrance in one building and connected to the dining room by an underground, stone covered tunnel. Despite the slight breeze and winter weather we opted to sit outside, tempted by the sound of waves and the glimmer of lights across the bay (although it wasn’t too lit up given Lebanon’s current situation).
For the mezze portion of the meal we opted for the classics, and were then brought to a tantalizing selection of fresh seafood. We selected only Lebanese fish, a larger one for grilling purposes and a variety of smaller fish to be fried. The mezze arrived promptly and we dug into an excellent spread of salads and dips. Both the fattoush and taboule were excellent, with fresh tasty vegetables and a generous addition of herbs. I was particularly a fan of the fattoush, with its hint of pomegranate molasses throughout. The only letdown was a platter of calamari - good enough but not particularly great, especially for a seafood restaurant of Babel’s reputation.
Unfortunately, the letdown we experienced with the calamari continued with the subsequent fish dishes. Neither the fried nor grilled fish were bad by any means, but they were equally unexceptional. A grilled seabream may have been overcooked, less flaky than expected, and on the drier side. The fried fish was better, but the oil had an aftertaste that may be reflective of overuse. Perhaps it was accentuated following the mezze, but my expectations for the fish were considerably higher.
At this point in the meal, it felt like the breeze had gotten stronger, so we decided to shift inside for dessert. The restaurant really is impressive, and I imagine visiting in the day, with a view of the sea would add to the experience. We were brought a tray of fruits and two different kinds of Lebanese desserts. I would say the dessert was the most disappointing part of the meal, and considerably less impressive than the mezze we started with.
Overall, Babel’s setting and mezze were fantastic but we were let down by the fish and the desserts course. Whilst I wouldn’t rule out a subsequent visit, my expectations given the restaurant’s reputation were undoubtedly higher.

column3: Abou Jihad Restaurant Jal el Dib
column9:
Place is a small restorant located near the main roads of jal el dib. With few locations to park and a valet service. You are welcomed with friendly staff. Locations require reservation since they are always crowded. At the time of the visit, the place was crowded.
Food took a while to be served.
Hummus: was good freshly made
Fattouch: lacks cucumbers and tomato came with big uncut green vegetables ( not fresh)
Sanbusik: came fried and well drained from oil, thin and crusty, but meat insert lacks flavour.
Spicy fries: well fried and came dried from oil crusty and good spicy combination.
Tawook platter: was about 2 shish of tawook with nothing else. Was well cooked jucy and well done.
Meat wrap: meat was well done and cooked, wrap came with meat hummus and few green vegetables, with lot of bread. Despite the excess, it was tasty.
Plase is known for his grill. They are always on point, but latley can be considered as pricy since portions are getting smaller.
Place is recommended for a takeout since atmospheres in restaurants are not the best too noisy and crowded.
Vegetarian options: There are some vegetarian options
Dietary restrictions: They have option for dietary persons with grilled options are the best.
Parking: Parking is hard to find, can park around 8 cars in front of restaurant which are almost always occupied
Kid-friendliness: No kids menue
Wheelchair accessibility: It is easily accessible since the restaurant is located at street level
column12: Abou Jihad Restaurant Jal el Dib_Fouad Houkayem_1

column9:
One of the best lebanese-cuisine restaurants in price/quality ratio to date.
It’s true that the atmosphere is nothing fancy, but the good-quality and fairly-priced food is definitely worth it.
It is also one of the most consistent places in quality and taste over the years. I have been going there close to 10 years and it managed to maintain high level of consistency.
Recommended dishes: generally all Lebanese mezzeh items (tapas) but also grilled meat, kabak and chicken taouk. The tablouleh, fattoush and rocca zaatar salads are always fresh and tasty.
I also like in particular how they make the traditional lebanese dish of fouwerigh (the only place I have it outside my mom’s kitchen!).
Vegetarian options: Plenty of vegetarian options

I recently visited Murray with a group of six people after seeing advertisements for the restaurant. Unfortunately, our experience was extremely disappointing. The service was very poor, with our waiter not paying attention to details. For example, when we ordered appetizers, they did not arrive together. When we ordered our main courses, another waiter had to come and take our order again because it had not been properly recorded.
We ordered the large fish plate and the large wings plate. The fish plate had a terrible smell and was almost inedible. The wings tasted like they were fried in old oil and were not fresh. When we asked our waiter about the fish smell, he called over the manager, who offered to pack the food for takeout since we did not want to eat it.
We mostly ate the fries, which were thankfully okay. I also asked for a San Benedetto bottle twice, but our waiter forgot both times. When I asked for it again while we were getting the check, he told me that it hadn't been charged yet. I told him that we had already left a tip of over 15%, taking into account the sparkling water bottle, but he kept insisting that it was not included in the bill. I had to wait for five minutes at the bar for the bottle.
To top it off, we were also feeling unwell the next day after eating the food. Overall, this was an extremely unpleasant experience, and I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone. Murray should take responsibility for their mistakes and train their staff better.

Decent food not wow; with perfunctory service.
SUD is hidden away up the stairs to the left of a small courtyard away from the street. Walking in it has a modern clean decor with outdoor seating upfront and in the back. We were seated quickly for lunch and ordered two appetizer, two mains and a dessert.
The shrimp avocado salad was fresh and the shrimp had a good char on them but the salad lacked in acidity. The beef truffle sliders were on the dry side but the sauce covered that up. The mushroom risotto and the beef fillet were decent but non memorable. The molten chocolate cake with a side of vanilla ice cream were well enjoyed along with a double espresso.
The service was rather perfunctory and not particularly quick or attentive, though always professional.
The overall experience was between three ans four stars, but we might give it another chance particularly when the weather is nice enough outside for outdoor dining.

column3: Rajasthan Al Malaki - Restaurant مطعم راجستان الملكي
column9:
Rajasthani cuisine is among those rare cuisines boasting of a never-ending platter with a plethora of dishes; ranging from tangy drinks to spicy starters, mouth-watering sabzis and variety of breads along with added delights of chutneys, achars, papad and chhach. Not to forget the delicate desserts that melt in your mouth instantly!
Being a Rajasthani I always crave for the peculiar taste and dishes and try and explore various restaurants for authentic rajasthani taste.
@rajasthanalmalaki serves decent, authentic and delicious vegetarian thali at a reasonable price.
The staff is very friendly and we love the overall experience.
They also have wide variety of sweets which are made of pure desi ghee, and their jalebis are really good and crunchy with that particular Indian taste.

And again i was back, this time for lunch as pre -bday celebration with the ladies!
The management, the service and the CHEF thank you for making it an enjoyable time regardless the poring rain.
We sat outside and were served by Peter and Yahia.
We started by the one and only addiction : tappenade and bread basket!
We ordered:
Green salad: we asked with extra cherry tomato and we so love the sauceeeeeee
Healthy quinoa salad again the sauce and the addition of pine nuts and the raisins
As main we shared:
- Grilled shrimps: a hit with its special the seasoning and the tartare sauce. The rice was not super though.
- Grilled salmon with a side of vegetables and fries accompanied with a lemon sauce.
- Asparagus risotto: creamy and cooked to perfection
And we ended it with dessert:
- Tartelette de chocolat: a mix of tarte and fondant so imagine the decadence of the taste it just melts in your mouth and the crunchiness of the tarte not to forget the vanilla ice cream on the side to contrast hot and cold!
- Maccaron au pistache: again not your regular maccaron: imagine a fuson of maccaron with a filling of cheese cake drizzled with a raspberry sauce and a scoop of strawberry ice cream
- Knowing me the more ice cream the merrier i am! SO i enjoyed sharing three scoops of chocolate, marron and mango!
I totally recommend you to visit the place; the service this time was way better and more professional We had lovely time.

column9:
Calling all Barbecue Lovers!
If you're in Jal el Dib, this place is a must-visit. We were a group of 19 people, mostly ordering sandwiches for our gathering. The delivery option was great, and the portion size easily fed all of us. The sandwiches arrived fresh and steaming hot.
Though we had a small issue with one sandwich, their customer service was excellent. When we contacted them, they quickly redelivered the correct sandwich without any trouble.
Now, about the food - I chose the meat (lahmeh) and chicken (taouk) sandwiches, and both were really satisfying. If you have a big appetite, I highly recommend trying the meat sandwich and sharing another flavor with a friend.
The restaurant specializes in Lebanese barbecue, and the sandwiches capture the delicious and rich flavors of the cuisine.
In conclusion, this place is definitely worth a visit. The overall experience, from the tasty food to the efficient service, leaves you with a positive impression. Check this place out; you won't regret it!

I visited this place after 22 years from initially going there. Little has changed in terms of the setup.
One major plus is being smoke-free. Even vapes are frowned upon.
I tried two dishes, chicken with cheese and chicken with lemon.
They both come with oven roast potatoes and a side of salad.
Portion size is very generous. They could easily trim the portions by a third and reduce the prices accordingly which are on the high side for Tripoli.
The food presentation is nothing to write home about.
In terms of flavour, it was a let down. The chicken with cheese was salty, creamy, lacking any chicken taste. The chicken with lemon needs to have less/no artificial lemon flavouring. Maybe they are using concentrated lemon juice.
The oven potatoes tasted and looked great but they were way hotter than the chicken in terms of temperature. And because of their proximity to the side salad, the salad became lukewarm.
I should point out that they serve a freshly backed loaf of bread with black olives. The olives come with vegetable oil or so it seems, ruining this experience from the get go. The bread is way too salty.
The staff were prompt and courteous. The smoke-free environment. These two saved the day.
The bathrooms are well kept. Expect to pay for valet parking even if you park yourself.
Parking: You could park up the hill away from the restaurant and take a short stroll if weather permits.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at O&C, and I must say it was an exceptional experience. Without a doubt, O&C is the best sushi place in Lebanon, offering the most trusted and amazing fish quality you can find.
One of the standout features of O&C is their generous sushi portions. Unlike many other sushi places, O&C doesn't skimp on the fish. It's not all rice; you can expect a generous amount of fish in each sushi roll, making every bite a delight.
The value for money at O&C is truly remarkable. For around $35, you can enjoy their open sushi option, where you can indulge in a wide variety of sushi rolls. If you prefer a la carte, you can enjoy a whopping 35 pieces of sushi for just $50. This is an amazing deal considering the high quality and freshness of the fish.
While the food at O&C is exceptional, I must mention that the service can be a bit slow. It took quite a bit of time for our sushi to arrive, which was a slight inconvenience. However, once the sushi arrived, it was definitely worth the wait. I hope that O&C can improve on this aspect and provide a more efficient service in the future.
Additionally, I noticed that the customer service at O&C could be better. The waiters seemed somewhat distant and lacked enthusiasm. They appeared to be a bit sad, low on energy, and sometimes even lazy. Improving the friendliness and attentiveness of the waitstaff would greatly enhance the overall dining experience at O&C.
Overall, I highly recommend O&C for their exceptional sushi offerings and the incredible value for money. Despite the minor drawbacks in service, the delicious and high-quality sushi more than makes up for it. Visit O&C for an unforgettable sushi experience in Lebanon.

I was finally able to make a reservation at this restaurant for yesterdays dinner and I can say no more than it was an amazing experience.
My first advice if you need to go you should make a reservation couple days ahead preferred 5 days minimum.
The cafe has a really nice, cozy and beautiful interior. The staff is very welcoming and friendly. Our waiter was amazing (mosheer) and very helpful.
The menu is really rich and variable. A must try is their turning shawarma on the deck and cheesy steak volcano.
The shisha was also very good.
I have two comments regarding : the taste of the fatouch platter that it can be upgraded if I was to compare it to the other fishes we tried. And the manager did not visit us at the table taking into consideration he did visit the tables next to our table.
They usually have a one man show on Fridays ( عود ) and he was really good. And another one man show on Tuesdays ( قدود حلبيه ).
This place is a ++++++ recommendation.
And will surly visit it again to try more of their platters.

Mayrig is a chic restaurant renowned for its Armenian dishes. It is located in the heart of the Beirut Gimmizeh quarter, well-known for its variety of restaurants and cafes.
The restaurant is housed in a heritage building and offers a range of indoor and outdoor seating options.

We opted for their salad collection platter, which offers a degustation of five Mayrig salads, then hummus with pasterma, potatoes, and finaly the famous Mante (an authentic Armenian dish of crispy beef dumplings, a hot tomato sauce, and cold yogurt),  which the waiter completes the mixture in front of you, adding a personal touch.
We finished our meal with the tasty dessert, Banirov Ma'amoul, which is composed of hot cheese Maamoul and homemade rose jam.
Strongly recommend.

Given the Armenian influence and sizable population in Lebanon, I was excited to try Mayrig, having heard several good reviews of the restaurant. As such, following a visit to the Arz in Barouk, my family and I decided to stop by on our way back from the mountains.
Visiting a few days after the New Year, the restaurant was busy, and had an inviting ambience. The building itself is beautiful, with stone walls and ornate designs on the floor. Nonetheless, we decided to sit outside, surrounded by an array of plants, and ordered a variety of recommended items.
The food itself varies slightly from typical Lebanese, with a noticeable affinity for sweetness through pomegranate molasses and cherries. The food arrived in waves, with an initial tableside spread of salads and dips, before we moved on to a series of main courses.
Most of the dishes were good, but short of excellent, although I was especially a fan of a yoghurt and kebab combination, a sour cherry kebab and a manti dish that was assembled tableside. The salads were slightly disappointing, and in some cases the dishes were slightly too sweet for my personal taste.
Overall, Mayrig provides an interesting experience with Armenian food. There were definitely some good dishes, and I enjoyed the atmosphere, but I left with my initial expectations not completely fulfilled.

INCREDIBLE VIEWS
The journey to mounir is just as beautiful as the destination, driving up the mountain on winding roads you get great views of Beirut,  the sea, and the traditional and modern architecture of homes built right into the side of the mountain. We went for lunch two days after Christmas at around 1pm, just before the big crowds arrived. During winter you have to sit inside, so some of the magic of the spectacular views is lost. Though they had beautiful Christmas decorations and the bathrooms were nice (ladies care about this) My highlight was the service was impeccable! All of the wait staff were very attentive. The meat hummus was yummy, but Ive had better mixed grill, this was served lukewarm and I like mine hot, sizzling and fresh off the grill. The Coteaux Lebanese red wine they served was delicious (I bought 2 bottles at the airport) and the Fattoush was to die for! Overall nice experience! Can’t wait to visit in summer!

As we approached, we saw a line (more like a cluster) forming on the pavement at the entrance of Swiss Butter. I thought to myself that this better be worth it. The manager was standing at the door, busily placing names on a waiting list. I added my name to the growing list. We were told that it was a 20 minute wait at most; true to their word, we were let in after 15. The waitress was cheerful and seemed to love explaining the eatery’s concept to first-time customers. There was no physical menu to hold in your hands, although the brief menu was enlarged and placed on the wall—the decor was akin to their menu: simple yet effective. She told us that it was one sauce that they made, and our choice of beef, chicken, or fish (in this case, salmon). A restaurant’s offerings relying on one specialty sauce was either a make it or break it situation. As we were waiting for our double order of medium cooked beef, I wanted in on the action of live cooking. So, after being granted permission to take photographs of their open kitchen by the restaurant manager, that is where I headed. Unfortunately, let’s just say that my enthusiasm was not appreciated by one of the chefs there. To sum it up, the photographs were hurried and Salted Caramel had turned bitter. Here, I would like to commend the extremely friendly manager and assistant manager who dealt with the issue in a swift and professional manner. My voice was heard and I was apologized to. Now, let’s get to the good part; the food. The beef was indeed grilled to a medium cuisson, and the tender result made me happy. The meat was accompanied with bread (one has the option of white or brown slices); they are that sure that you would want to savor every drop of their sauce by smearing your bread in it. Also, alongside these constituents were crispy french fries and a fresh salad. Ok, let’s get back to the beef smothered in that sauce of theirs. The liquid goodness is delicious, and has exactly the right amount of tang. Honestly, I do not know if it would go as well with the chicken or salmon; I’ll have to give them a taste to find out. However, the sauce with the beef was a match made in heaven. I was so glad that there was a generous amount of sauce to cover your meat and then dip your fries in. I really enjoyed the food and my taste buds were very awake. I thought that it was impossible for them to be awakened any further at this restaurant, but I was wrong. The dessert options are also limited, but like the savory offerings, that was more than enough. We ordered the pain perdu and the molten chocolate, both of which came in a pan just as the meat had come in before them (maintaining the theme). The molten chocolate dessert is to die for. It is delectable; both the cake and the gooey insides are amazing. As for the pain perdu, the caramel with the sauce and melting vanilla ice cream mixture was really good too—but that molten chocolate confection! At the end of the meal I was full to the brim, and to our surprise, the desserts were not added to the amount due on the bill. All in all, Swiss Butter proves that you do not need an extensive menu to succeed, as long as the items you have are done really well. I would definitely go again.

After having been to this place several times few years ago, what I witnessed today was very unexpected. The service was extremely poor comparing to how it used to be as well as the food quality. We ordered a smoked salmon platter along with a mushroom and pepperoni pizza and the order came wrong.
First, the salmon had a very low quality it was dark as you can see in the picture as well as a bad after taste. The waiter got us a margherita pizza instead of a mushroom one and told the waiter to add some mushroom on it to fix the issue instead of making us a fresh proper mushroom pizza. We then kindly asked them to make us a new order. The pepperoni pizza was overly burnt and the cheese was not fresh at all it was very chewy.
Overall, all I can say is that the service and quality of food has strongly and sadly shifted backwards.

From the moment you step through the doors, you're greeted with a friendly welcome from the efficient staff, setting the tone for an exceptional dining experience. The cozy atmosphere envelops you, creating the perfect backdrop for indulging in a culinary journey like no other.

As you make your way to the restaurant area, you're presented with a menu that promises culinary delights beyond compare. Each dish is a masterpiece, carefully crafted to tantalize your taste buds and leave you craving for more. From traditional Lebanese mezze to innovative Mediterranean creations, every plate is a testament to the culinary prowess of the chefs at Mezyan.
What truly sets Mezyan apart is its commitment to providing top-notch service at reasonable prices. Despite its reputation for excellence, Mezyan remains accessible to all, ensuring that everyone can experience the magic of its cuisine.
Adding to the allure of Mezyan are the occasional bands that grace the stage, entertaining guests with soulful melodies and infectious rhythms. It's the perfect accompaniment to an already unforgettable dining experience, elevating it to new heights of enjoyment.
In addition to its regular offerings, Mezyan also caters to tailor-made events, ensuring that every celebration is imbued with the same level of care and attention to detail that has become synonymous with the restaurant.
Whether you're dining solo or with a group, reservations at Mezyan are highly recommended to ensure you secure a spot in this culinary paradise. The restaurant attracts a diverse clientele, with both locals and foreigners from all walks of life coming together to savor its delights.
In conclusion, Mezyan Restaurant is a true gem in the bustling neighborhood of Hamra. With its delectable cuisine, cozy ambiance, and top-notch service, it's a place where culinary dreams come to life. Whether you're a seasoned food enthusiast or simply looking for an unforgettable dining experience, Mezyan is sure to exceed your expectations.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Mezyan, a hidden gem of a mezze restaurant tucked away in Beirut, and let me tell you, it was an experience to remember. From the moment I stepped through the doors, I knew I was in for something special.
First and foremost, the food at Mezyan is simply outstanding. Each dish burst with authentic flavours that transported me straight to the heart of Lebanese cuisine. Paired with some delightful local wines, every bite was a culinary adventure that left me craving more.
But it's not just the food that makes Mezyan stand out - it's the atmosphere as well. The restaurant boasts an authentic design that captures the essence of Lebanese culture, creating a warm and inviting ambience that instantly makes you feel at home. Sure, finding the place might be a bit of a challenge, as you need to enter via the big hall of another building, but trust me, it's well worth the effort.
One dish that particularly stood out to me was the kibbe - it was simply amazing. Perfectly seasoned and expertly prepared, it was a true testament to the skill and dedication of the chefs at Mezyan.
Of course, great food is only part of the equation - service is equally important, and Mezyan certainly delivers in that department. The staff were attentive, friendly, and knowledgeable, ensuring that every aspect of my dining experience was nothing short of perfect.
And let's not forget about the prices - for the quality of the food and service you receive, the prices at Mezyan are incredibly smart. You'll leave feeling satisfied both in your stomach and in your wallet, which is always a win in my book.
In conclusion, if you're looking for an unforgettable dining experience in Beirut that combines amazing food, an authentic atmosphere, and excellent service, look no further than Mezyan. Trust me, you won't be disappointed.

Located in the heart of the city, our favorite Lebanese high-end restaurant offers an unparalleled dining experience that tantalizes the senses from start to finish. From the moment you step through the elegant entrance, you're greeted with an ambiance that seamlessly blends sophistication with warm Lebanese hospitality.
The menu boasts a diverse selection of traditional Lebanese dishes prepared with the finest ingredients, each dish a masterpiece of flavor and presentation. Whether you're indulging in savory appetizers like hummus or savoring the succulent grilled meats, every bite is a culinary delight that transports you to the streets of Beirut.
But it's not just the food that sets this restaurant apart; it's the impeccable service that truly elevates the dining experience. From the knowledgeable waitstaff who are eager to guide you through the menu to the attentive servers who ensure your glass is always full, the service here is nothing short of exceptional.
And let's not forget about the shisha, which adds an extra layer of enjoyment to the evening. Whether you prefer classic flavors like apple, lemon and mint (our favorite) or more exotic blends, the shisha here is expertly prepared and provides the perfect accompaniment to your meal.
In conclusion, our favorite Lebanese high-end restaurant is a culinary gem that never fails to impress. With its outstanding cuisine, impeccable service, and inviting atmosphere, it's the perfect destination for any occasion, whether you're celebrating a special milestone or simply indulging in a night out with friends.

Although Em sheriff is known to be one of the nicest restaurants in downtown Beirut, I hadn’t gotten around to visiting until recently.
We got several dishes from the menu, all of which tasted wonderful. The dandelion, the liver, the mtabbal, and the ghazal dessert in particular stood out. The food was just incredible.
We also got a dessert that came in jar, I don’t remember the name of it but we found it rather bitter and would recommend people avoid it (I think it may have been the Aish Al Soriya)
The service is super quick, even when the restaurant is busy.
The restaurant does take credit card, which is rather rare in Lebanon after the banking crisis.
Reservations are required if you want to eat before 9:30 PM, so call in advance to set one up.

I've visited this location twice. The service is good and reasonably fast. The place is big, open, and very clean.
I prefer the wedges over the fries as once they get cold, they get kinda hard and aren't very good, in my opinion. The bread they use for the clubs, although very toasted, somehow stays soft enough to enjoy without being poked in the gums by hard pieces. The only issue with the club is that after your first bite, you need to use a fork as the filling pretty much falls out. It's not a big deal, but it's good to note for messy eaters.
You get carrot sticks and a nut/snack mix as a sort of appetizer. ***Note: The carrots get a healthy squeeze of lemon juice, which surprised me the first time.
If shisha is your thing, you may enjoy it, be it inside or outside. Like most places, you can also smoke cigarettes inside.
I would recommend and return. Enjoy!
Parking: There is a paid valet parking lot right across the street.
Kid-friendliness: It is very kid friendly, but do note that there could be a lot of smoke from cigarettes and shisha when it's very busy.

I had to write a review about Provincial in Antelias because it was just fantastic! We ordered a whole bunch of stuff to share, and everything was so fresh, it felt like they picked it straight from the garden.
The salads were incredible. We got a quinoa salad and a kale salad, and the dressings were delicious - not too strong, not too weak, just perfect. They definitely didn't skimp on the ingredients either, everything tasted top-notch.
We also tried the tomato bruschetta and the halloumi bruschetta. Both were amazing, especially the bread - you could tell it was freshly baked, warm and soft. The wedges were a hit too, super crispy and addictive.
The whole restaurant had a great atmosphere. The music was nice and relaxing, and we sat outside surrounded by trees. It felt like a little oasis in the city. Our waiter, Elie, was awesome - really friendly and helpful.
The prices were very reasonable relative to the huge portion and especially compared to restaurants in Beirut.
Overall, Provincial is a must-visit!

Bou Melhem is a very good choice for Lebanese food lovers where they would enjoy their food within a very fair budget in a pleasant and very entertaining setting.
Once there do not miss the followings:
• Tabboule, Raheb salad (revisited), muhmmara, a succulent homemade marination of stuffed wine leafs, hummus with grilled walnut mixed with rocca, and a fine raw Kebbe made of prime meat.
• batata harra (a very "delicate" plate in terms of frying and definitely the best one can have today over the market), chicken marinated liver, a filet "ras asfour" with cashew nuts, almonds and mushrooms, and a chicken pesto plate with pine nuts.
• their heavenly assortment of grilled meat, ribs, taouk, kafta and kebab all cooked to perfection and a MUST TRY 👌
We spent more than 3 hours at Bou Melhem without noticing it! On a thusday night, the place hosts a professional violinist à-la-Rieu who magically transformed the entire environment into a superbly cheerful yet classy one by playing a repertoire of recognizable russian and lebanese folklore songs.
Bou Melhem hosts entertaining programs every tuesday (oud) thursday, friday and saturday that deserve to be applauded. Note that these are totally for free, and that no additional fees are paid by customers for entertainment.
Definitely Recommended.

Zomato and The peninsula management hosted us, a bunch of eager foodies, for a zomato meetup.
Escape the city's traffic and disconnect, how you may ask? Well it is easy.
The peninsula is located in Dbayeh back street before Le Royal Hotel. Take a small turn on the right to be transported to field of gardenia and cheerful smiles.
Behind the big wooden door you enter the villa where attention has been given to the details to stay faithful to the Italian theme.
Walk even further and there you will find a terrace looking over the garden where they host on Thursdays themed nights animated by dancers and a lavish buffet of Italian delicacies.
Now back to the essential, the food experience!
First things first; the warm bread basket / box wrapped with green cloth and served with a side of marinated tomatoes: et voila you can make your own fresh bruschetta!
The menu had different kinds of salads:
Insalata della casa: a beautiful presentation and rich ingredients, though I always prefer the cherry tomatoes over regular ones. The balsamic vinaigrette complemented it perfectly
Insalata iceberg: chopped into four  portions and drizzled with a Roquefort sauce with crunchy walnuts
Tartare di salmone con salsa limone: one of the best I ever had, the slight peppery kick it has makes all the difference alone with the freshness of the salmon
Insalata di gamberetti con mozzarella: again attention to the details in the presentation that leaves your mouth-watering and your belly satisfied with a non-deceiving taste
Melanzane alla sorentina: in a clay dish, and though I avoid fried food, but this dish is rich and is worth the try, a non oily fried eggplant covered with marinara and dense cheese.
Bresaola al limone: served as a flower with a center of radicchio leaves, yes flavorsome!
For the pizza I picked the goat cheese and sun-dried tomatoes and could not be happier with my choice. A thin crust and delicious fillings
Homemade cut by hand fresh crunchy golden fries; need to say more?!
As main courses we shared:
Filetto ai porcini: I modified the sauce to make it a la mustarda! The meat is succulent and cooked as per my request medium rare. It literary melts under your mouth; however I would have preferred the same veggies served with salmon and maybe grilled rosemary potato wedges!
Salmone alla griglia: flaking off the fork and served with broccoli, mushrooms and baby corns
The floor and marketing managers were the sweetest addition to this eve. Besides the tour they gave us around the restaurant areas, they insisted that we taste almost all kinds of desserts they serve and we could not be happier:
The apple pie: my favorite layers of caramelized apples and alot of cinnamon served with their homemade vanilla ice cream and drizzled with caramel sauce
The crème brulée: I did not imagine to be a fan: a crunchy caramelized sugar topping beneath it a custard mix and a sweet taste
Chocolate fondant: the delicious volcano releasing the black lava we all crave! oh not to forget the ice cream scoop
The Italian staple: Tiramissu, I liked it but though could use more creaminess maybe?
Thank you guys for the high standard service, the tasty food and the pleasant conversation.
And my lovely readers, what are you waiting for, pick up the phone and reserve asap to the cheapest trip to Italy!

After a nearly whole year hiatus, Iris opens its doors, hoping to revive the energetic night vibes and chill sunsets it's famous for. Sadly, Iris' return underwhelmes and looses some of its charm in the process.
I called ahead and reserved a dinner table for two. I explicitly asked for a table sitting and not bar seats. The phone operator definitely assuaded my concerns, assuring me that I'll be getting a table sitting as long as I order dinner and drinks.
Come the evening, they sat us at the bar (to clarify, I was aiming for the small high table seats, not the big central ones). When I addressed the issue with the manager at the check-in desk, he proclaims, and I quote: "Iris is no place for couples' dinings. And tables are reserved for groups of 4 people minimum". His delivery of the line was pretentious and needlessly arrogant. Anyway, I'm the bigger man, so I take the seats at the bar, which aren't too bad. The bartender was very kind and welcoming.
On to the menu. There isn't much in terms of variety, prices are some of the highest in Beirut, and the portions are comically small. Credit where it's due, what was served was good tasting. Still, the portions wouldn't satiate a famished patron.
The music was nice, and the volume level was just right and balanced. The scenery was beautiful as it's always been.
All in all, a somewhat positive experience that's definitely a step back from the standards Iris itself had set in the past.
My advice is to take the manager's advice to heart. Dine elsewhere, and come enjoy the scenery and vibes over a couple of good drinks at the bar. Even if you're well off, other places have better value at more reasonable prices.

During my recent visit to S&1/2, I had a mixed experience. While the food was very good, there were some issues with the service. This was my first time at this branch, and there were so many orders and noises that it was difficult to enjoy the atmosphere. We ordered the chicken escalope sandwich, shawarma shaker, and fries box, all for $10. Before we ordered, the staff told us we would have to wait 30 minutes, which was okay with us. We placed our order at 8:48 pm.
At 9:02 pm, the sandwich was done, and at 9:27 pm, the shaker was done, which was surprising since shakers are supposed to be a fast meal. All of our orders were being prepared for delivery, which may have contributed to the delay.
While the food was tasty, I found the sauce to be spicy. It would be great if the restaurant could take into consideration that not everyone likes spicy meals. Also, the fries were good, but the portions were small. Overall, I had a mixed experience at this restaurant, but I would be willing to give it another try in the future.

I absolutely adore Bar Tartine! After being abroad for some time, I was thrilled to return and find that the restaurant still maintains its exceptional quality and taste, if not even better. From the moment we stepped inside, we were greeted with warm smiles and a welcoming atmosphere. The interior design is chic and modern, with stylish decor and comfortable seating arrangements that immediately put us at ease.
Our waitress, Setrida, was an absolute gem. She displayed a perfect balance of professionalism and friendliness, taking amazing care of us throughout our visit. She patiently answered all our questions about the menu and provided excellent recommendations based on our preferences. Her attentiveness and genuine interest in ensuring our dining experience was top-notch made us feel valued and appreciated as customers.
Now, let's talk about the food. Oh my goodness, it was beyond delicious! The menu offers a diverse range of options, from classic favorites to creative and innovative dishes. Each bite was a burst of flavor and a true delight for the taste buds. The attention to detail in every dish was evident, and the presentation was nothing short of stunning. We couldn't help but savor every moment of our meal.
Despite the incredible quality of the food, the bill was surprisingly reasonable. Considering the portion sizes and the level of craftsmanship that goes into the dishes, we felt like we were getting exceptional value for our money. Bar Tartine truly understands the importance of providing an affordable yet memorable dining experience.
One aspect that stood out to us was the cozy and inviting atmosphere. The lighting was soft and warm, creating a relaxed ambiance that was perfect for a casual catch-up with friends or a romantic date night. The restaurant was bustling with a lively energy, yet it never felt overcrowded or noisy. We were able to enjoy our conversations without any distractions, allowing us to fully immerse ourselves in the dining experience.
In conclusion, I highly recommend Bar Tartine for brunch, lunch, and dinner without a doubt. It is a haven for food lovers, where exceptional quality, attentive service, reasonable pricing, and a cozy atmosphere come together to create a truly enjoyable dining experience. Whether you're a local or a visitor, Bar Tartine is a must-visit destination that will leave you wanting to come back for more.

I recently visited Amar seaside restaurant in Antelias and unfortunately, I was left disappointed. Let's start with the main issue - the price. I simply cannot justify paying almost $100 for a meal for two people, especially when the quality and taste did not match the high price tag. We ordered a shrimp fatteh, an octopus provencial, along with regular appetizers and a small plate of minced beef with cherry. However, despite the variety on the menu, everything turned out to be quite mediocre.
On a positive note, I must admit that the service was satisfactory. The staff was friendly and attentive to our needs. Additionally, the restaurant offers beautiful views from its terrace, especially if you choose to dine by the beach. This added to the overall ambiance of the place.
One thing worth mentioning is that Amar seaside restaurant also serves shisha. If you're a shisha enthusiast, this may be a good option for you.
In conclusion, while Amar seaside restaurant has its merits such as decent service and pleasant views, the high price and mediocre quality of the food left me feeling dissatisfied. For the price we paid, I expected a culinary experience that would exceed expectations. Unfortunately, that was not the case. If you're looking for a luxurious dining experience, be prepared to spend a significant amount here. They were nice to offer us dessert and fruits at the end.

column9:
Came here for dinner on a Monday night at 6pm. It’s a great location and easy to get to whether you are staying on Elephantine island or on mainland. Our motorboat driver dropped us off here upon request. They have lots of tables with views of the Nile. We had no wait grabbing one. However because the restaurant was busy, waitstaffs were sometimes hard to get their attention. The food is good and fair priced for the location, ambiance and food offered.
We ordered a hibiscus drink, guava juice, Nubian milk tea with cardamom, camel meat tagine, fried chicken and Nubian desert. The tamarind drink was not available at the time. Our total was 805 EGP for 2 person.
Surprisingly our food came out within 15 minutes of ordering. I was expecting to wait an hour. The hibiscus drink was a bit too sweet for me. The milk tea was good and the guava juice was fresh. You can hear them blending the juices. The camel meat tagine was amazing. It tastes just like beef with no gamey taste at all and it was so tender. My fried chicken was actually a grilled leg of chicken. It didn’t have enough seasoning but the skin was crispy which I liked. The meals also came with a side of potatoes and peas tagine. They also came with a tomato and cucumber salad, which had a very light, to no dressing, bread, seasoned rice and tahina. The Nubian pie for dessert was just ok. It’s like puff pastry layered with sweet milk. It came out piping hot. It was not sweet enough though and could use some spice like cinnamon or cardamom to really take it up a notch.
Their bathroom is clean. They had bug zappers which was nice. They also offer hookah. They take credit cards and I heard their breakfast is also good from another customer.

Highly recommended.

He was attentive and friendly and we enjoyed being taken care of by him. We each ordered something different - salmon, grilled chicken tenders, pepper steak, Mexican spaghetti - and each thoroughly enjoyed our meal. The 6 oz grilled tenders doesn't look like much but it is quite satisfying and delicious! I highly recommend it. The cheese bread was yummy, and our water was very watery. Just what you would expect. :) we enjoyed listening to a variety of music piped through their speakers from pop to Christian music, and appreciated their mission to glorify God and serve Him through service to their customers. That's very impressive, especially since they really do model that mission well. On the way out we were touched to see New Testaments out for anyone who may desire a copy. The atmosphere was cozy and we would love to come back, possibly on our way back home.
Oh, and the fireplace was pretty. 👍

I recently had the pleasure of dining at an Egyptian restaurant that truly transported me to the heart of Egypt's culinary delights. From the moment I stepped in, I was enchanted by the warm and inviting atmosphere that enveloped the entire space.
Let's talk about the food—it was exceptional in every sense. Each dish was a work of art, meticulously prepared with authentic Egyptian flavors and spices that tantalized my taste buds. The Oxtail was succulent and bursting with flavor, a testament to the chef's mastery of the grill.
What truly elevated my dining experience was the impeccable service. The staff were not only attentive and knowledgeable about the menu but also exuded a genuine passion for sharing their culture through food. Their recommendations were spot on, and they went above and beyond to ensure that every aspect of my meal was perfect.
The atmosphere of the restaurant was another highlight. The decor transported me to the bustling streets of Cairo, with vibrant colors, intricate patterns, and soft Egyptian music playing in the background. It was the perfect backdrop for a memorable dining experience, whether you're looking for a cozy dinner for two or a lively gathering with friends and family.
In conclusion, this Egyptian restaurant is a gem that deserves to be celebrated. With exceptional food, great staff, and an amazing atmosphere, it's a must-visit for anyone craving an authentic taste of Egypt's culinary heritage. Special thanks to Yaseer , Emad and Amr.

So we had this run away trip from Beirut's traffic. We spotted Sandwich w nos Mansourieh on our way and gave it a try...
We ordered this lovely six wheel burger and a kafta sandwich.
Taste: The taste reminds me of the childhood burgers we used to have and this lovely home taste and the kafta was awesome too.
Presentation: Not really wow but fair enough for such a concept.
Service: to that I give 5... The cashier missunderstood my special request and when I was served with my wrong order, the cashier professionally and politely insisted on fixing it and that was great. On the other hand, there is this guy who has an eye on the tables at all times and serves you with wipes and toothpicks the moment you are done before immediately clearing the tables.
Price: I believe that for a taste like that and such a service, the price is fair.
Cleanliness: It should be a bit better than that, but its nothing that serious. Maybe the washroom needs a bit more attention but its not dirty, still fine.
I recommend it for a fast bite but not for a classy or fancy dinner.

Honestly, go to fazolis you’ll leave more satisfied for half the price.

The service was great; our waitress was a trainee and she did everything just right. She was professional and friendly, and worked efficiently. The ambiance was nice, although a tad noisy. For my meal, I had the Salmon & Couscous platter this time, and I loved it. The salmon was succulent and majestically stood on a bed of extremely soft and fluffy couscous. I enjoyed the delicious pairing of fish and fluff with each bite. It made me want to come back again to try more dishes, and maybe also brunch.

I was not overly impressed (although the wait & # of people that kept coming in indicates it must be better than my experience)
Waited about 15 minutes beyond our initial 20 we were told, and had to wait quite a while just to order a drink. *I got 'carded' haha so maybe I should increase my ranking.
Finally ordered, our poor waitress was obviously new. I asked if the deluxe salad came with green peppers (she didn't know). But since the house salad was described as 'lettuce only', I felt the need to go deluxe to get some carrots and other extras.
Our salads finally arrived. They were loaded with green peppers (chopped into fine pieces which were not easy to pick out). It also had white onion.  I love onion, but actually despise white onion in my salads.
After about 5 minutes of digging, I tried to eat my salad. I just couldn't. The best thing on it was the single small lonely pepperocini.
Salads finished our waitress stopped to inquire if I had ordered broccoli.  Unfortunately they were out....
Our entrees arrived and were very attractively plated. My vegetable subbed was green beans, it was a toss up for me... I couldn't decide if the green beans or that lonely pepperocini was the best thing I ate.
My husband was starving, so he scarfed everything down. The bread (garlic cheese?), the salad, and his spaghetti (spicy he said).
Our waitress was doing the best she could (and was super polite). Everyone was welcoming & friendly.
Just not sure I would go back.

column9:
What a lovely way to wrap up our visit to Aswan than with a quick boat ride across the river to the charming King Jamaica restaurant. Offering a great selection of Nubian cuisine (at reasonable prices) with a gorgeous view of the river Nile, this is one of the best spots to enjoy a sunset meal.
Best dishes have got to go to the camel curry tagine and the stuffed pigeon, and they can whip up a decent vegan option upon request too.
Especially fun was the low cushioned balcony seating upstairs, would recommend in case it's a bit windy, and finishing your meal with a spiced Nubian coffee.
Overall a great meal with great service from this family run restaurant, that also really makes you feel part of the family. Can recommend!

1. They managed really bad the timings:
14.01h an appetizer is served
14.09h the mezze is served
14.20h the main dish is served
15.05h the dessert is served (45 minutes after the main dish, absolutely out of compass, especially after being so quickly with all the others)

Good at:
Atmosphere. Place is quiet, perfect for maintaining a good conversation without having to scream. Also well decorated
Staff. They are kind
Views. Some tables have really good views over the Nile

A lovely place down by the river. Even when everywhere else seemed quiet this place was busy with both locals and tourists which is always a good sign. Service was very quick and professional - no hidden charges.
We shared a few dishes: tahini, garlic bread, chicken shawarma, baba ganoush and tomato soup. A mix. The tahini was nice and seemed fresh, shawarma was very tasty but the fries with it were cold. The soup was nice and tasty and the ganoush also. Garlic bread a bit disappointing - I wouldn’t have ordered this again. It seemed like a store bought loaf with some cheese and pepper over baked on. Felt cheap when the free bread they gave with the tahini was far nicer.
Views of the Nile are there, but not remarkable. You’re mostly blocked by a group of feluccas and taxi boats.
Overall a good restaurant and we would definitely return.
Kid-friendliness: Not built for kids but not really bad for them either. There were some there with no issue.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this lovely establishment, and I must say, it was a delightful experience. The food here is authentic and made with fresh ingredients, just like my Egyptian mother and grandmother used to prepare. We tried the beef, chicken, and apple salad, and they were all delicious. The meat was tender, and the flavors of the vegetables and spices complemented each other beautifully. The rice was also well-made, reminding me of the rice dishes I enjoyed in Egypt.
The portions were generous, ensuring that we left satisfied. We also ordered the ice cream with dadels for dessert. What an original and lovely dessert this was.
Karim, the owner, is clearly passionate about his food, and it shows in the flavors. He and his team provided excellent service, and their dedication to the culinary experience was evident throughout our visit.
One aspect worth mentioning is that the restaurant operates on a slow cooking concept, which means the food is prepared hours in advance. This speaks to their commitment to freshness and quality. So make sure to make a reservation.
Another highlight is that the salads are fresh and won't cause any stomach issues, which is a welcome change. It's refreshing to find a place where you can enjoy a salad worry-free.
In conclusion, this restaurant offers a delightful dining experience with authentic flavors and fresh ingredients. I recommend making a reservation and enjoying the culinary delights prepared by Karim and his team.

5 star should be the rating  for the good service provided by Tito. Very attentive and caring . 3 star for the food. We choose the beef fillet served on the hot stone  , ok the beef is local. The cut was very odd. Maybe the head of fillet and not the center. Also the meat is not aged therefore was very chevy and not particolarmente nice in taste and texture  also the fillet is served as a whole piece. It is very well equipped from cheese fondue casserole and warmer to the added spice and rock salt and fine pepper and you can easily read between the lines.

I was really sorry that we hadn't enough time to try desserts but i am sure they will be great.
The quality of the food is incomparable to any place in Egypt.
The money is a bit on the upper side but for value it is great.

This place is a real Italian gem on a relatively quiet street. After having Egyptian food at least once a day for the past 5 days, we decided to look for some other cuisine to try, and thus stumbled across Pizza Roma. The service was great, the ambience perfect for a quiet dinner, and the food Mamma Mia! was simply superb! So much that we dined there 2 nights in a row. Here's what we ordered and loved - Penne Arrabiata, Profondo Rosso pizza, Quatro Cami pizza, Speciale Piccante pizza. The portion size is perfect and we love how they could further spice up our dishes on our request. All in all, we highly recommend them to everyone visiting Luxor!
Vegetarian options: They have lots of vegetarian options in pizzas and pastas, as well in appetizers.

Jeeda's has one of the nicest atmospheres I've seen in any upscale restaurant in Alexanderia. The decor is very pleasing to the eye, the music is enjoyable without being intrusive, and the seats are quite comfortable.
The staff are incredibly nice and helpful. Every member of staff we talked to was very very nice to us and we would like to thank each of them personally.
That said, the food was quite underwhelming. We went at a time where it was quite quiet, so there was no rush, but the food was barely good nonetheless. I ordered Pollo Al Ajillo, which arrived barely lukewarm. The chicken breasts were overcooked and chalky. The dish was also bland, but I presume that's because they want their customers to salt their plates to taste, so there is no shame about that (fresh pepper and salt were provided at the table). The french fries side was excellent. Beautifully crisp on the outside and fluffy on the inside. I also got a strawberry watermelon lemonade, which was definitely really good too. I paid about 500 EGP total, which I find to be quite steep for overcooked chicken.

One word. Amazing.
Let's get one thing out of the way, ignore the decor! It's some kind of fake cave ,with red balloons. Doesn't really relate to the rest of the experience. Now that we got this point out of the way, I absolutely recommend this place!
We had a seafood feast. Grilled shrimps, crabs and lobsters. All marinated in a special but not overpowering taste. A seafood cup for a starter tasted quite rich, more like a chowder in thickness and full of flavor. My friends had shrimp tageen with bashamel , and eggplant tageen with shrimps, both were well received.
I mentioned my gluten allergies and the chef sent the waiter with further questions about my allergies,  I really appreciated the attention for details and the sincerity. He made me a special version of the soup without flour, and sent the waiter with information about which plates are safe for me and which to avoid. He also made me a special gluten free version of the lobsters , without the flour containing sauce.
The waiter was friendly, informative and funny, in a sincere way and not overly hovering like some tend to do.
The food was well balanced,  tasty and not one plate was a dud. Absolutely talented chef , and well chosen staff. Highly recommended
Parking: Parked in a pay by the hour parking

Set El-Beet translates into English as ”lady of the house”.  The name is accurate, as local Fayoum women prepare the food lovingly and expertly in the kitchen. It has the home made taste of yumminess- traditional recipes Egyptian mama’s have passed down for generations.
The garden where you sit and eat is peaceful and quiet. The waiters are friendly and eager to practice their English.
We ate the molokhiya, chicken and rice, and fish. Everything was delicious.
For a relaxing and fulfilling meal I recommend coming here. You will get the taste of Egypt paired with the peace of Fayoum.
Highly recommended.

All burgers are served with Some salad on the side and Mustard.

Also,the consistency is too gooey, the balance between the supposedly mascarpone (didn’t taste like it) and the savoiardi is off. To add insult to the injury, I couldn’t taste the coffee which is pretty much the base of this dessert.
I’d be happy to make them some of my tiramisu, it’s pretty simple you just need the right ingredients.
- The music on weekdays doesn’t add to the vibe/identity of this gem in Alexandria, it’s as if someone searched “White people’s top 50” on Spotify and put them on repeat. Would be nice if there were more original music that add to the whole Mediterranean vibe.
- I heard people complain about the prices, but that’s the price you pay for the best food in town! The pricing is equivalent to average prices in Europe and the US, although this aint New York but it’s still def worth it for me.
Conclusion: This gem definitely deserves the five star rating in spite of the distressing Tiramisu, everything else makes up for it!
As her highness, Lady Gaga once said:
-BRILLIANT -INCREDIBLE -AMAZING -SHOW STOPPING -UNIQUE -SPECTACULAR -NEVER THE SAME
Keep going Jeeda’s!

During my visit to Nişantaşi Restaurant in Cairo Festival City Mall, I had the opportunity to try their Fettuş Salata, Nişantaşi Meze, and Karışık Izgara, and I must say the food was delicious.
The Fettuş Salata was fresh and flavorful, with a delightful combination of ingredients that pleased the palate. The Nişantaşi Meze offered a variety of tasty options, showcasing the restaurant's skill in preparing Mediterranean appetizers. As for the Karışık Izgara, it was a highlight of the meal, with a well-grilled assortment of meats that were tender and full of flavor.
The restaurant's attention to detail in the presentation and taste of the dishes was evident, and the quality of the food was commendable.
However, I found the prices to be a little on the higher side, considering the portion sizes and overall dining experience. While the food was undeniably excellent, it would be more satisfying if it were slightly more affordable.
On a positive note, the bread served at Nişantaşi Restaurant was perfect, fresh, and complemented the meal wonderfully. The attentive staff members provided friendly service throughout my visit, further enhancing the dining experience.
In conclusion, Nişantaşi Restaurant at Cairo Festival City Mall offers delicious food, particularly the Fettuş Salata, Nişantaşi Meze, and Karışık Izgara. While the prices may be a bit high, the quality of the dishes and the attentive service make it a worthwhile choice for a flavorful dining experience.

Okay, so I’m not too keen on Sea Food but this was easily one of the best restaurants I visited on my trip through Egypt.
I didn’t pick a meal from the menu, but I was asked to hand pick from a selection of fresh fish! The interior is great, colored lanterns cast dancing shapes as the wind gently pushes them. And just like the other restaurants the sea view is great.
The food was expertly prepared and I was given everything I needed to enjoy the fish to the fullest. I wish every restaurant provided a whole bowl of lemons to season the food with!
The service was impeccable, with tea on the house, a traditional Egyptian hand washing session and even a plant sprayer to deter hungry cats from snatching your meal.
In conclusion: this was the best seafood I ever had in my life. I quite some time after my meal to keep enjoying the atmosphere and if I had more days in Dahab I’d definitely come back for more!

We went to Shark since it's ranked the highest amongst the sea line restaurants.
Instead of choosing dishes from the menu (that would probably be a bit cheaper) we took the waiter's advice (he calls himself Shahar after an Israeli comedian that looks like him), and took a 2 Kg Seafood platter of 250g fresh lobster, 250g octopus, 250g calamari, and some 12 prawns, half grilled and half sauteed. We paid 2000 Egp.
The dish was big and very tasty, a bit overcooked to my personal opinion but well seasoned.
There are a couple of very recommended seafood places that are not on the sea line so they focus only on the level of food, but sitting above the waterline and watching the full moon shimmering on the water definitely made a difference.
Recommended, and they have no hidden costs like other places do (billing for the bread and salads).
Kid-friendliness: The team was very nice to the girls
Wheelchair accessibility: The have a ramp and broad passage between the tables

If you're in the Dahab area and looking for a seafood restaurant, look no further than this gem that my wife and I have found. We keep coming back because the food is always fresh and incredibly delicious.
The seafood options are particularly noteworthy - it's clear that the chefs only use the freshest ingredients, and the taste reflects that. I highly recommend trying the homemade pasta (seafood pasta or royal seafood pasta) as well - it's a standout dish that's cooked to perfection.
One thing that sets this restaurant apart is the service. The staff are friendly, welcoming, and attentive to detail. They go out of their way to make sure you're comfortable and satisfied with your meal.
If you're still hungry after your main course, I highly recommend the Apple Crumble - it's a perfect ending to a delicious meal.
While you're waiting for your main course, the restaurant serves a series of small plates with different toppings to put on a piece of freshly-baked bread. It's a nice touch that keeps you from getting bored while you wait for your meal.
Finally, if you're a seafood lover, you'll appreciate the restaurant's display of the day's catch. You can choose the exact seafood you want, which is then expertly prepared by the chefs.
While this seafood restaurant is truly exceptional, it's worth mentioning that there is one potential downside: cats. While the restaurant itself is clean and well-maintained, there are cats that sometimes lurk around the outdoor seating area. This can be a bit distracting or even upsetting, especially if you're not a fan of cats or simply allergic.
In fact, during our last visit, one of these cats tried to steal my wife's shrimp and ended up scratching me when I tried to intervene (help, in fact). While this was a bit of a negative experience, it's important to note that it didn't ruin our overall enjoyment of the meal.
Additionally, it's worth noting that if you're planning on visiting this restaurant during busy Israeli public holidays or any other holiday, it's highly recommended to reserve a table in advance due to the high demand. This is a popular spot among tourists, so it's important to plan ahead if you want to ensure you have a table.
Overall, this seafood restaurant is a must-visit for anyone in the Dahab area. The food is exceptional, the service is warm and attentive, and the atmosphere is perfect for a special occasion or a casual night out.

column9:
The place is pretty but that’s pretty much the only good thing about it.
It wasn’t authentic Turkish food at all.
And service was very off.
It started at the beginning when the lady in front kept insisting we give her a phone number. We don’t like sharing our info with anyone and that’s our right. But she kept insisting and for the most random reason “in case we need to call you if you forget something”.
We ordered a salad which came out super salty. When we told them about it, they tried to play it off as “this is how it is”.. no I don’t think salad comes out this salty.
It also had something very hard that my husband bit on and they also tried to play it off as the burghul (which should be soft anyway).
The other thing we ordered were the lamb chops. Again, bit into something very hard. And the meat was a bit over cooked. Flavor-wise it wasn’t bad though.
The rice was very greasy.
The Pide bread itself was good but the meat and cheese weren’t impressive at all.
The person taking our order wasn’t the nicest and had a bit of an attitude when we had comments and remarks, as if he took it personally. He also took the tahina plate before we could finish it and he didn’t even ask if we were done with it.
When the manager came, he tried to make it seem like we didn’t understand what the food should be like.
The price did not reflect the value of the food at all. Way overpriced.
It all looks pretty but when it comes down to taste, service and price for value (which are all things a restaurant is built on) it’s a big disappointment.
Wouldn’t go there again unfortunately.

The restaurant's location is amazing. The view is so beautiful.
The service is a bit slow and got really careless when a small group of people came despite it was only us and them.
The prices are a bit overly priced as the portions were relatively small ( see pictures below). The meat was a bit overly cooked so it was dry even though with sauce as it was so dry that it was kinda hard to cut it down with the knives.
The salad was average neither good nor bad.
We had Pizza Napolitana wich came after over an hour and was so salty! And the waiter's had it with absolutely no tableware and he was surprised that we asked for extra plates! I think he expected us to eat straight from the main plate with our bare hands!
But we ate it anyway as we we're hungry.
We ordered Pinacolada which was so light you can hardly taste any coconut in it.
The Way to the bathroom had the sewers overflowing on the whole ground and had a terrible terrible terrible smell almost nauseating! Even after reporting that, they let it dry on it's own which was really disgusting.
As for value vs money, it's a little over priced since the quantity is really small and below expectations.
The view was the best thing honestly.
If you're looking for a place to grab a drink by the sea with great view it's really good to relaxe, otherwise not so much.
Tip: ( call first to reserve even though the restaurant was practically empty, yet they had us stay at the hotel's gate even though we booked but someone forgot to mention our reservation to the security. So call, AND double check first for your names so you don't have to wait 15 minutes to get in.)

column9: This place because of their simply scrumptious food and their service deserves nothing less than 5 stars. On the last day of our tour, our tour guide took us here to treat us to another amazing Egyptian lunch - we were a small group of 5 including the guide and his driver. Not sure what the dishes are called in Arabic but here's what we ordered and simply loved - macaroni bechamel, beef and onion stew (came with white rice), grilled boneless chicken shish tawouk with rice and fries, salad, pickled eggplant, tahini, babaganoush, their special baked bread, cabbage rice, etc. Everything was delicious and we were really spoilt by the manager Mr. Saleh Al Oswani as at the end we got to try their kunafa and basbousa for dessert on the house along with some other delicacies. It's definitely a must-visit restaurant, very close to the Nile! Whenever we are back, we will definitely be dining again here.

This bar/restaurant is accessed through the Bella Vista Resort reception. Head straight down through the gardens keeping to the left side and keep going until you reach the beach. Where it will be visible.
It is a decent enough looking place, comfortable and on the edge of the sea. Taking this into account the prices are sort of reasonable, since they include all taxes but not tips. This is stated on the menu.
I just popped in for a cold beer and a snack to test the kitchen.  A Meister Max at 70le and a Melanzane Bruschetta at 45le. The beer was cold and crisp and was served with a frosted glass. It didn't take long to get warm but the staff brought me ice on request, with no issue.
The Bruschetta was fresh and warm but utterly tasteless. Woefully under seasoned with no garlic to be found anywhere and not a hint of olive oil or any herbs. Bland and immediately forgetful.  If they are unable to make a simple bruschett, I would be concerned about ordering anything more expensive from the menu.
The service is relaxed, as the food comes from La Luna restaurant which is attached to the front of the hotel. 30 minutes for a bruschetta. Any dishes that I saw, looked well presented and appetising. But then, so was my tasteless bruschetta!
1 star down for my food. Otherwise a great but not inexpensive watering hole.
I have added pictures of the menu for your perusal.

Sofra is my favourite restaurant in Egypt without question. The food and drink is flavourful and delicious, and everything they give you is completely fresh. Id throughly recommend the Tagin Lahma Bil Kawerma (Veal and pearl onion Tagin) and Shakshuka for mains among other amazing options. Definitely try the Sahlab (an Egyptian drink made from milk, orchids and nuts) or the range of fresh fruit juices to drink.
The atmosphere is lovely. The top floor where we ate is naturally airy (helped at your discretion by fan and air conditioner) and cool, and the decor and furniture are beautiful. The waiters are friendly and attentive, and will answer any question asked in English. Absolutely a must visit if you’re in Luxor and want to experience Egyptian cuisine.

With such great reviews by so many sites and here in Google Review, expectations were high. Sadly, it's probably average at best. And in some areas, truly disappointed for such an upmarket pricing.
Surprisingly quite empty when I came at about 5pm on Tuesday. Only 1 other table was occupied.
Firstly, the server who took our order was extremely arrogant, claiming that all the dishes are very good when asked for recommendations. I though he was kidding but he was not saying this with a smile at all. Mentioned this several times without any help nor guiding us on how best we could make our choices. Even walked away and asked us to think about what we wanted. He disappeared thereafter. Worst service ever. Other servers are much better.
The it was the food. Generally not too bad but definitely not up to the rave reviews. The lamb in lamb shank casserole is indeed tender, but I didn't like the flavoured rice. A bit too moist and the taste does blend well. Stuffed baby aubergine and bosara was just OK.
The other main problem is the cleanliness. When you run your finger on the table or even the salt shaker, you can feel a layer of dust. This is definitely unacceptable for a restaurant at this price range. Don't the wipe their table after each customer?
I certainly wouldn't recommend this place.
Wheelchair accessibility: None. Stairs even to the ground floor dining area.

Nestled in the heart of Luxor, Sofra stands out as a culinary gem, offering a captivating journey into the rich tapestry of Egyptian flavors. From the moment you step through the doors, the beautiful tiles and authentic decor transport you to the heart of Egypt, setting the stage for a truly memorable experience.
The attentive and knowledgeable staff adds to the welcoming atmosphere, making you feel like an honored guest in a friend's home. We especially thank Ragab for making us feel special.
We indulged in the mezze platter, a delightful array of small dishes featuring classics like baba ganoush, hummus, and falafel. Each bite was a burst of freshness and flavor. We then had moussaka which was a delight after a long day exploring the beauties of Luxor. The chefs at Sofra take pride in using high-quality, locally-sourced ingredients, and it truly reflects in the taste and presentation of every dish.
Sofra's commitment to authenticity extends beyond the menu to the restaurant's ambiance. The decor is a thoughtful blend of modern elegance and traditional elements, creating a space that is both inviting and culturally immersive.
In conclusion, Sofra is not just a restaurant; it's a culinary journey through the heart of Egypt. The dedication to authenticity, the impeccable service, and the exquisite flavors make it a must-visit for anyone visiting Luxor.

Sofra is a victim of its own success. It has potential to be great - but it’s way too popular (definitely make a reservation, many people were turned away) and the staff can’t keep up.
The good: Staff were friendly, the restaurant set up is beautiful with antique furnishing, they have a wide variety of juices and the fresh lemon juice was yummy. Food wise, we enjoyed the baked lamb kofta - delicious, cooked perfectly so the meat wasn’t dry. The prices are really affordable and fair.
The bad:
- We were seated in a small room next to the entrance, which made us invisible to staff and it was really stuffy when the front desk guy closed the doors, we asked for it to be opened up to get some air conditioning from the bigger room. Unfortunately another Indian family was also seated in the room across us, as only the European guests were shown upstairs for seating.
- The wait time. It took 30 minutes for our drinks to arrive and a total of 50 mins for our food - which was considered fast as we walked up to the front desk to ask to place our orders instead of waiting in the room. The Indian family waited 40 minutes to just place their orders.
- Unfortunately they forgot my lemon juice order initially
- The food was disappointing. The chicken tajin had chicken fried separately and placed on top of the stew instead of being cooked together. Perhaps they had no time - chicken was dry and the stew was tasteless. The fried prawns were a little salty and the rice was hard and tasteless as well.
To be fair, the kind front waiter noticed we didn’t finish our food and asked for feedback. I showed him the dry chicken and he waived it off the bill.
Perhaps the good reviews here are from tourists who haven’t tasted great Egyptian food - there’s way better restaurants such as Loqma and El Kebabgy.
If the Sofra kitchen can’t keep up with the orders, close some of your rooms and limit the number of guests so the quality of food is good.

Cannot recommend enough, the staff were so friendly and professional, we were never with an empty glass or extinguished Shisha, It was our last night in Hurghada so we decided to go to a fancy restaurant for drinks, dinner and Shisha, the location was very nice with a view to the beach and the Red Sea, we ordered a red wine, an Alabama Slammer and two fresh juices (orange and a guava) My friend was happy with the wine and with it being my first time trying Egyptian wine I was pleasantly surprised, The Slammer was close to perfect and set me up grandly for dinner, The juices were both very fresh and cold. Onto dinner I thought I would try the Paella, It was out of this world, A delightful Egyptian spin on a Spanish classic, was extremely happy with this, and as my friend and I were having seafood we went for the Ayam white wine, it was very good and went down a little too easy even though I am not usually fond of white wine, after a delicious meal we moved back out to the balcony for another bottle of Ayam and a Shisha, The Shisha was the best I’ve tried and lasted a nice long session, Kareem was very attentive and mixed a lovely Shisha and we weren’t without a smoke the rest of the evening, after being there about 5 hours in total and a bottle of wine each we decided to move on to a nightclub so out came the bill and I was very surprised at how so well priced the evening was, between the two of us the total came to about E£4500 (about £40/$50 each) for this type of service, quality and location/atmosphere I would have gladly paid double, this place is not to be missed if you are in Hurghada, Shout out to Harry who made us very welcome 100/100

DISCLAIMER - Be Aware of Fake Reviews. I found many fake reviews, so try not to fall into their trap.
I assisted my friend in ordering Indian food since she is a big fan of Indian food and always try while travelling. But after listening to her experience of having dinner here, it is the same as an unexpected nightmare.
The following reason I would like to list here about experience -
1) The food was not at all good in taste. To be precise, the food was not at all in condition to eat for a normal human being. It was too salty to eat one bite of it. (Even Can't finish all the food due to bad taste)
2) the staff behaviour was awful. They were behaving like they were serving food free of cost. And their attitude was very disgusting- they wanted my friend to eat and go go quickly.
3) My friend did not finish the food, and the staff came to clean the table. I don't know which country's presidential election he was going to contest 🤷
4) the only thing my friend liked about the restaurant and could enjoy was water because it was not made or cooked or packed by them.
5) I would not deny the class of ambience of place, but the pathetic behaviour of the staff and the staff themselves made it awful.
6)the restaurant name is 'Namaste" and it is a word from Hindi, Indian people use it as greeting at the time they meet or leave. The meaning of the word is I bow and pay respect to the inner good of you. But sadly I have to say that not a single person obey this term and made felt very disrespectful.
7) After 12 hours of having food in this restaurant, my friend is having stomach ache and diarrhoea. She even doesn't feel good at all even after 48 hours. So keep your health in priority and avoid going there.
Conclusively, I would suggest do go to this place if you are in good mood or want to enjoy your time and the occasion.
And I expect some decency from the owner that he or she will put a little effort into making staff behave well with visitors.
