When you are looking for somewhere to go out for a meal, location plays a huge part in the decision making process (most of the time).
On this occasion our choice in Hurghada was to go to Granada. Our friends were over from the UK on holiday and we were sure that they would appreciate the stunning view from the terrace.
This restaurant is located on Old Sheraton Street on a hill with uninterrupted views over the Red Sea. You couldn't pick a nicer place for the view in my opinion.
There is an enclosed air-conditioned dining area, but why would you want to sit in there when you could choose the terrace with comfortable sofas? OK, the tables are quite low to be eating at, but when you get to enjoy your meal with these stunning views you can't complain.
It's not my first time to eat here. In the past I've not really been impressed with the food especially at the price you pay as its not cheap here. They also sell imported alcohol, so a real Tia Maria and Coke went down really well, I considered it a treat.
Since our last visit the menu has been changed. There is still a massive selection but it's more up to date.
We thought the food was good and the portion was more than enough. There was just one thing that we couldn't unders6, although the food was good, it was all sweet. The chicken and beef Fajita had a sweet after taste to it and so did the Chicken & Veal Schnitzel.  I think the chef maybe should taste what is being served. It wasn't bad  but it had an interesting taste that was not really our cup of tea.
Another interesting choice was the sides for the Schnitzel.  They were served with tomato Spaghetti (the tomato sauce was sweet) and a baked potato. We asked if we could change the Spaghetti and Baked potato to French fries and vegetables,  but we were told we couldn't which was a shame,  especially for the price paid. Carbs on top of carbs makes it a very difficult and heavy meal to eat.
The Shrimp spring rolls were lovely.
We did enjoy our meal here, and we will be back. Its a lovely place to meet friends and unwind.

When you are looking for somewhere to go out for a meal, location plays a huge part in the decision making process (most of the time).
On this occasion our choice in Hurghada was to go to Granada. Our friends were over from the UK on holiday and we were sure that they would appreciate the stunning view from the terrace.
This restaurant is located on Old Sheraton Street on a hill with uninterrupted views over the Red Sea. You couldn't pick a nicer place for the view in my opinion.
There is an enclosed air-conditioned dining area, but why would you want to sit in there when you could choose the terrace with comfortable sofas? OK, the tables are quite low to be eating at, but when you get to enjoy your meal with these stunning views you can't complain.
It's not my first time to eat here. In the past I've not really been impressed with the food especially at the price you pay as its not cheap here. They also sell imported alcohol, so a real Tia Maria and Coke went down really well, I considered it a treat.
Since our last visit the menu has been changed. There is still a massive selection but it's more up to date.
We thought the food was good and the portion was more than enough. There was just one thing that we couldn't unders6, although the food was good, it was all sweet. The chicken and beef Fajita had a sweet after taste to it and so did the Chicken & Veal Schnitzel.  I think the chef maybe should taste what is being served. It wasn't bad  but it had an interesting taste that was not really our cup of tea.
Another interesting choice was the sides for the Schnitzel.  They were served with tomato Spaghetti (the tomato sauce was sweet) and a baked potato. We asked if we could change the Spaghetti and Baked potato to French fries and vegetables,  but we were told we couldn't which was a shame,  especially for the price paid. Carbs on top of carbs makes it a very difficult and heavy meal to eat.
The Shrimp spring rolls were lovely.
We did enjoy our meal here, and we will be back. Its a lovely place to meet friends and unwind.

A casual and homey bar restaurant. It's great to have Czech draft beer at a reasonable price.
You can enjoy authentic Czech cuisine (mainly meat dishes).

In particular, the garlic soup is a must-try dish.
The owner's family, including the husband, wife, young lady, and friends, are all really kind and nice people. Of course, the staff is friendly and you can enjoy a pleasant meal.
Quite often, I get delivery food from the nearby Japanese restaurant Kawa in Prague, and the collaboration between Czech draft beer and Japanese food is truly amazing♪
Thank you so much, Prague Family!

We were a small group of friends having dinner, so we had the chance to share and try many plates in the menu, and here is my opinion :
Cold Appetizers : 4/5  (Muhammara is the best and I'll give it 5/5)
Hot Appetizers : 5/5 we had Kibbeh with pine and Karisik Pide
Main Dishes : 4.5/5 , we had different kinds of grilled meat and chicken , most of them were very good , except the lamb chops (kuzu pirzola) those were really amazing and deserved the 5/5 , also we had a very beautiful dish , we've been told it's one of their best sellers the "Beyti Kebab Sarma" , also was perfect and deserves the 5/5.
Drinks : we all took the Ayran Milk , and that will take 4/5 , it was perfect and fresh , but really over priced , also 45 L.E. for a bottle of water ?
Desserts : the most disappointing items of the visit , and the only reason why i give the whole experience a 4/5 only , the Baklava With Pistachio and Dandurma  2.5/5 , the Bourma cheese kunafa 3.5/5 at most , also exceptionally high prices , 130++ for one peace of average baklava or small plate of cheese Kunafa?
Totally , The place is excellent , serving real Authentic Turkish Food , Extremely Clean , Prices are above average as expected -with few notes on some side items & desserts prices- but generally acceptable , considering the high quality food and the professional, fast, helpful and friendly team working in this beautiful and beautiful vibes .
Very Recommended to visit , and definitely we will come again ISA.

column9: Our first night in Aswan, we took a private boat ride with Momen to Bob Marley Moonlight Terrace. The boat ride was very safe, professional, and fun. My recent visit to Basta Restaurant Qatar with my friend Rhys, who hails from East Asia, was nothing short of spectacular. We sampled two dishes, Sheykh Al Fareij and Machboos, and were blown away by the culinary prowess showcased in each plate.
First and foremost, the food at Basta Restaurant is simply incredible. It ranks among my top dining experiences, thanks to the exceptional flavors and quality ingredients. The Sheykh Al Fareij and Machboos were both cooked to perfection, with the meat being a standout element that left us speechless.
The ambiance of the restaurant is noteworthy as well. Adorned with captivating posters and pictures from bygone eras, Basta Restaurant exudes a charming and nostalgic vibe. We opted to sit outside, enjoying the pleasant weather, but I would recommend indoor seating during the summer months to avoid discomfort.
We complemented our meal with Leban, a drink reminiscent of what we call Dough in my country. The refreshing taste added to our overall dining satisfaction. The rice accompanying our dishes was cooked impeccably, adding a delightful texture to each bite.
One aspect that stood out was the presentation of the food. The way the dishes were served showcased a blend of aesthetics and attention to detail, enhancing our dining experience.
To top it off, the visit from a restaurant supervisor added a personal touch. Their inquiry about our satisfaction with the food and the staff’s hospitality further emphasized the restaurant’s commitment to customer satisfaction.
In conclusion, dining at Basta Restaurant Qatar was an absolute pleasure. We left the restaurant with content hearts and happy taste buds, thoroughly enjoying every aspect of our experience. I highly recommend Basta Restaurant to anyone looking for a memorable culinary journey filled with exquisite flavors and a welcoming atmosphere.

It requires reservation of table for dining. I had reached at almost restaurant closing time. Ms. Sara and her colleague gave a warm welcome and they both were very generous in making me comfortable and trying their best to arrange me a table. Mr. Danish was assigned for my table. He was very humble and polite and welcoming. Danish suggested me a vegetarian option as I wanted to eat veg cuisine. I loved the aunthetic Iranian (Persian) food , it had all the love and delicacy that I had not tasted anywhere in Qatar on my work trip. I was glad that Sara could arrange a table and Danish recommended me the Korak cuisine. It was very kind of restaurant to provide Salad with cheese and walnut and olives along with Bread. Loved the Ambience, Atmosphere, Cuisine, People and most importantly the vibes of this place that makes you feel special. It is not at all expensive. It's Worth it. I would recommend this place to everyone, I wish I could have more days and could come here each day to eat such delicacy. Loved it. Thank you once again Sara and Danish for this beautiful experience.
Vegetarian options: Veg Korak is amazing.

Beautiful restaurant in Souq Waqif but as others have mentioned, you do need to make a reservation as they get really busy. We had to wait around 20mins to be seated even when we had a booking.
The decorative setting does make for some wonderful holiday pictures and whilst the food was good, it wasn’t the best we experienced in Doha.
Value is not bad for somewhere this popular - our bill for 2 of us came to around QAR230 (approximately £50) - this was for 2 x main courses and 2 x Pepsi’s. The complimentary Arabic breads and salad with cheese, olives and walnuts that’s served once you’ve ordered was a lovely little touch.
Definitely worth visiting if you’re in the area.

I recently had the pleasure of visiting MADO, a Turkish restaurant located in the Pearl, and overall, I was quite impressed with my experience. The restaurant boasts a cozy atmosphere, with stylish decor that transports you to Turkey. The service was excellent, with friendly staff who were attentive and made sure my dining experience was enjoyable.
Now, let's talk about the food. I decided to try their breakfast menu, and while it was quite pricey, it was definitely worth it. The standout dish for me was the traditional Turkish breakfast platter, which was a combination of various cheeses, olives, honey, and bread. It was a delightful feast for the senses and left me feeling satisfied and happy.
However, there were a couple of downsides to my experience that prevented me from giving MADO a perfect rating. Firstly, the prices were quite steep, which may not be affordable for everyone. Additionally, the portion sizes were on the smaller side, so I didn't feel like I got as much food as I would have liked for the price I paid.
Overall, I would highly recommend MADO to anyone who's looking for a unique dining experience in the Pearl. The food is delicious, the service is great, and the atmosphere is cozy and inviting. Just be prepared to spend a little more money than you would at other breakfast spots in the area. I give it a solid 4 stars out of 5.

Nestled in the heart of Doha, Trader Vic's offers an exquisite dining experience that is truly unparalleled. From the moment we arrived, it was clear that this was a high-end establishment, boasting an elegant ambience and a menu that reflects its upscale nature.
The highlight of our visit was undoubtedly the food. We had a specific request for our dishes to be prepared extra spicy, and the attention to detail was impeccable. The manager himself came to our table to confirm our preference, ensuring that our culinary experience was tailored to our tastes. This personal touch set the tone for the evening, showcasing their commitment to customer satisfaction.
Each dish we ordered was a symphony of flavours, expertly crafted and beautifully presented. The spice level was exactly as requested, adding an exciting kick without overpowering the nuanced flavours of the cuisine. It was evident that the chefs at Trader Vic's take great pride in their work, resulting in dishes that are both creative and delicious.
The staff were exemplary, providing attentive and knowledgeable service throughout our meal. Their professionalism and enthusiasm enhanced our dining experience, making us feel well-cared for from start to finish. Their ability to provide detailed information about the menu and make thoughtful recommendations was greatly appreciated.
In conclusion, Trader Vic's in Doha is a top-tier restaurant that delivers on all fronts. From the sophisticated setting to the flawless execution of the dishes, it is a destination for those seeking a memorable dining experience. While the menu is on the pricier side, the quality of the food and the outstanding service make it worth every riyal. If you're in Doha and looking for a place to indulge in a luxurious meal, Trader Vic's is the perfect choice.

Four of us enjoyed dinner at Trader Vic's yesterday. Definitely a favorite restaurant of ours when we've got Entertainer vouchers to use.
Strengths: all food we ordered was very tasty. Amongst us, we had the short ribs, the flambee, one of the fish dishes and the filet steak. The macadamia asparagus and the flambee were especially delicious. They also serve my favorite cocktail of all time - the famous chi chi. As we went during happy hour, the drink was 50% off.
Drawbacks: the food is over priced for the portions you get, especially with the flambee. However, the Entertainer does make the prices much more reasonable. Service for the flambee was not table side (more like "table adjacent" which means the showmanship associated with a flambee is lost). The service was quite slow at the end, but it was always friendly. I get it... They don't want to push you out rudely. But my husband actually had to kind of shout "excuse me" to a waitress because she was chatting with the dudes behind the bar and never turned around.
Summary: overall, the place is really nice and worth it. The happy hour and nibbles at Tahitian Village is even better (just next door). If you've got the entertainer, definitely stop by for dinner.

The Cheesecake Factory offers a delightful dining experience with a wide variety of options that cater to diverse tastes. During my recent visit, I was impressed by the expansive menu that spans multiple cuisines, ensuring there's something for everyone.
The ambiance is warm and inviting, with a stylish yet comfortable decor. The lighting and seating arrangements create a pleasant atmosphere perfect for both casual outings and special occasions. The staff were friendly and attentive, making sure we felt welcomed and taken care of throughout our meal.
For appetizers, we tried the Avocado Eggrolls and Fried Macaroni and Cheese. Both were delicious and set the stage for what was to come. For our main courses, we opted for a variety of vegetarian dishes. The Veggie Tacos were flavorful and well-seasoned, with fresh ingredients that made every bite enjoyable. The Vegan Cobb Salad was a standout, packed with a medley of vegetables and a tangy dressing that tied everything together perfectly. Evelyn’s Favorite Pasta was a hearty and satisfying dish, loaded with vegetables and a light garlic sauce. The Veggie Burger was also excellent, with a well-seasoned patty and a delicious blend of toppings.
The highlight, of course, was the cheesecake. We chose the Oreo Dream Extreme Cheesecake and it did not disappoint. The rich, creamy texture combined with the crunchy Oreo pieces was heavenly. It was the perfect ending to our meal.
We walked in without a reservation and experienced a wait time of about 15-20 minutes. While this was a bit of an inconvenience, it was understandable given the restaurant’s popularity. Additionally, while the portion sizes are generous, the prices are on the higher side, making it a bit pricey for regular dining.
Overall, The Cheesecake Factory provides a fantastic dining experience with delicious food, great service, and a welcoming atmosphere. It’s a wonderful place to enjoy a meal with family and friends, and I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a memorable dining outing.

I recently visited Cheesecake Factory at Villagio Mall after a day’s work at Khalifa International Stadium, and I must say it was a satisfying experience.
The location of the restaurant within the mall made it easily accessible, and the short walk from the stadium was convenient.
Upon arrival, we were greeted at the welcome desk and promptly seated at a prepared table. The efficiency was appreciated.
We opted for Spaghetti with Meatballs and Fish and Chips along with 2 servings of Coke Zero. The spaghetti, though presented beautifully, had a rather ordinary taste. The meatballs, however, were unexpectedly large, which was a pleasant surprise.
The highlight of our meal was the Fish and Chips, which were exceptionally delicious. The flavors were spot on, making it the standout dish of our visit.
One notable aspect was the refillable soda, allowing us to enjoy unlimited drinks throughout our meal.
Before the main dishes, we were served two types of fresh bread with butter, which we thoroughly enjoyed.
Overall, Cheesecake Factory offers a good dining experience with a diverse menu selection. While some dishes may be average, others like the Fish and Chips make up for it, ensuring a satisfying visit.

Situated in the vibrant Villagio Mall, Asha's offers a delightful escape into the rich and aromatic world of Indian cuisine. Our visit to this esteemed restaurant left us thoroughly impressed, from the impeccable service to the exquisite flavours that define its menu.
We had a specific request for our food to be prepared extra spicy, and the manager's personal attention to this detail was a commendable touch. He came to our table to double-check our preference, ensuring that our dining experience would meet our expectations. This level of attentiveness is a hallmark of Asha's exceptional service.
The food at Asha's was absolutely perfect, showcasing the true flavors of Indian cuisine. Each dish was a testament to the high-quality spices and meticulous attention to detail employed by the chefs. The extra spiciness was perfectly balanced, enhancing the dishes without overwhelming the inherent flavors. Every bite was a celebration of authentic Indian tastes, crafted with skill and passion.
Despite being located in a bustling mall, Asha's maintains a serene and inviting atmosphere. The menu is reasonably priced, making it accessible without compromising on the quality of the dining experience. The staff were on point, offering informative and friendly service that greatly enhanced our visit. Their knowledge of the menu and thoughtful recommendations were particularly appreciated.

Whether you're a local or a visitor exploring Villagio Mall, Asha's is a must-visit destination for a memorable meal.

I recommend anyday.

I went to the branch at Doha Festival city and decided to try out the cheesecake factory, I have tried it multiple times already but not at this branch yet, safe to say customer service was on point as the server was really friendly and helped us at all the requests we wanted. The pasta that I took was delicious, I loved the texture and the portion was enough, there was an option for dinner which was bigger but Lunch option was more than enough for me as I did not want to get way too full. Our dining experience at the Cheesecake Factory was a mixed bag. Starting on a high note, our server Aiko was the highlight of our evening. Her infectious personality and exceptional service made us feel truly welcomed. She was chatty, funny, and extremely helpful, with a warm smile that never left her face. In terms of service, the rating was an undeniable 10/10.
Moving on to the food, things got a bit rocky. We ordered a kids' meal pepperoni pizza, which was nothing short of a disappointment. The cheese was watery, greasy, and the overwhelming garlic smell was off-putting. Unfortunately, the child in our party found it unpalatable, which led us to cancel the order. The pizza, sadly, was a dismal 1/10.
However, the restaurant redeemed itself with the beefsteak taco meal. The dish was flavourful and delivered a delightful explosion of good flavours on the palate. It was apparent that Cheesecake Factory maintains consistency in the quality and taste of this dish, earning it a well-deserved 9/10.
The Skinnylicious turkey and avocado sandwich was another high point of our meal. The excellent quality turkey, soft milk bun, and fresh avocado made for an excellent sandwich. It was a hit and a definite 10/10.
The final dish we sampled was the fried shrimp, which unfortunately fell short. While the flavors were there, the shrimp was undercooked and crunchy. The sweet and sour sauce had an unusual plastic-like taste, which was off-putting. The accompanying coleslaw was overly sour, further detracting from the dish. I will give it a rating of 3/10 and that's being generous.
In conclusion, our experience at Cheesecake Factory was a roller coaster of highs and lows. While the service was impeccable and a couple of dishes impressed us, the inconsistency in the quality of food was significant. We hope the Cheesecake Factory takes our feedback into consideration and improves upon the areas that need attention.

Our dining experience at the Cheesecake Factory was a mixed bag. Starting on a high note, our server Aiko was the highlight of our evening. Her infectious personality and exceptional service made us feel truly welcomed. She was chatty, funny, and extremely helpful, with a warm smile that never left her face. In terms of service, the rating was an undeniable 10/10.
Moving on to the food, things got a bit rocky. We ordered a kids' meal pepperoni pizza, which was nothing short of a disappointment. The cheese was watery, greasy, and the overwhelming garlic smell was off-putting. Unfortunately, the child in our party found it unpalatable, which led us to cancel the order. The pizza, sadly, was a dismal 1/10.
However, the restaurant redeemed itself with the beefsteak taco meal. The dish was flavourful and delivered a delightful explosion of good flavours on the palate. It was apparent that Cheesecake Factory maintains consistency in the quality and taste of this dish, earning it a well-deserved 9/10.
The Skinnylicious turkey and avocado sandwich was another high point of our meal. The excellent quality turkey, soft milk bun, and fresh avocado made for an excellent sandwich. It was a hit and a definite 10/10.
The final dish we sampled was the fried shrimp, which unfortunately fell short. While the flavors were there, the shrimp was undercooked and crunchy. The sweet and sour sauce had an unusual plastic-like taste, which was off-putting. The accompanying coleslaw was overly sour, further detracting from the dish. I will give it a rating of 3/10 and that's being generous.
In conclusion, our experience at Cheesecake Factory was a roller coaster of highs and lows. While the service was impeccable and a couple of dishes impressed us, the inconsistency in the quality of food was significant. We hope the Cheesecake Factory takes our feedback into consideration and improves upon the areas that need attention.

Contemporary fine-dine restaurant established by our beloved Asha Bhosle. The rich spices and aroma of the food was unmatched. The tender meat slipping through our fingers and melting in our mouth is a moment to experience.
I couldn’t get over their Pressure cooked Lamb curry along with a bowl of Jasmine rice which was suggested by our host. Its a must try, REALLY. The lamb was cooked to everyone’s liking and the aromatic curry filled our hearts.
The Murgh Kalimirch had soft chicken pieces with crispy onions and as we had ordered mild spicy dishes, they had done a pretty good job.
Along with the two gravy based dishes, we ordered a naan basket which consisted of garlic butter naan, butter naan, roti and plain naan.
As a rice option, we weren’t sure we would finish it. But it was sooo delicious and yummmm, we couldn’t help it but completely finished the kadai😂 We had ordered Kesar Mutton Biryani. The caramelised onions and tender mutton pieces cooked along with kesari milk not giving a sweet base but a mild spicy one was just perfect.
They have their restaurants in a mall setting so its not much of quiet and peace but they do have good seating arrangements and decor in their space. I have come across their restaurant in Villagio and Doha Festival City. The hosts are happy to serve you and have really suggestions, so don’t forget to ask them.

Doha Festival city was the family’s choice to do some shopping and a pre-valentine dinner was on the schedule. We decided to go to Cheesecake Factory after years of not dining there.
My daughter had the Corn dog and the bowl of Mac n Cheese. They were both good but the Mac n cheese was too hot during service. My daughter had a hard time eating it.
My wife had the Burger Spring rolls and Quesadillas. The spring rolls were aptly named. It was like having a burger on a wrap. The portions were very generous as the beef was heavy on the tummy. The quesadillas were also good. Though there was nothing extra ordinary tasting about it.
I had the Korean fried chicken. This dish was a bit interesting. The flavors on the chicken were very tasty. It was complimented by the sides of guacamole and kimchi. It gave the unique oriental taste being a Korean fried chicken.
Dessert was the best part. We had the Cinnabon cheesecake. The portion was really big. We shared 1 slice and we enjoyed. It was not too sweet and overpowering. The cinnamon seasoning was not too strong. It was a great overall experience.
In general, it was a safe choice to have good food.

Since Wok of Game started several years ago, we debated about going there and didn't. At the end of 2021, we finally decided to step in. After a long wait of 45 min, we were able to go to our table upstairs.
Various options were available in the buffet, but there was none at the Live stations like that of Sushi.
Some popular choices were being refilled often. Our fav were Chicken Lollipop/skewers, fried fish, fried rice and the grilled chicken.
We didn't get to sample any other seafood though as it was emptied out. The Beef dish was ok, just a bit bland.
The choices were several and the place seems to be very popular. The price is decent and the service is wonderful too.
If you choose to go there, book ahead and go early, so that you get to sample all of their food.

Overall, our experience at Bennigan's was mixed. The ambiance of the restaurant was nice, and there was a playground nearby which was a great plus for families with young children. However, the food did not fully meet our expectations.
On the positive side, the Mix & Match plate we ordered Boneless barbecue wings and Buffalo Wings were flavorful and enjoyable. The Irishman Glazed Burger was a highlight of the meal, with its layers of homemade Irish glazed burger, sauteed onion, cheddar cheese, beef bacon strips, and toasted brioche bun. The taste was balanced and satisfying, and the pickles and homestyle French fries that accompanied the burger were also quite good.
Unfortunately, our green salad arrived without dressing, which was a disappointment. Additionally, while the Irishman Glazed Chicken sounded promising with its basting and glaze, we found it to be lacking in flavor. The roasted garlic mashed potato and roasted vegetables were okay, but not particularly memorable.

column9:
Fuefo sushi restaurant review
In Zamalek
The pictures of the place suggest extreme luxury, but the level of the place on the ground is simple luxury
The place is very small and the seating areas are cramped
There are three types of soup, and the miso soup does not contain tofu, and I did not order it for this reason
There are two types of salads available: salmon tartar and tuna, and there is no Crispy Crab salad, which is considered basic in most Japanese restaurants.
The fried appetizers are many and varied and their quality is high 👌 and I recommend trying them
There are many types of sushi, and the menu is easy and convenient, as it clearly explains the shape and ingredients of each type. The problem is that the menu is in English only, as if sushi or luxury food is exclusive to those who speak English (and by the way, I have a bachelor’s degree in English) 😂
The important thing is that I liked all the types of sushi I tried
I ordered two types including mango
There are types with avocado and cream cheese, and with shrimp, tuna, and salmon, and I liked all of them 🍣👌
I consider it a restaurant that specializes in sushi and appetizers, especially tempura fries
Prices are relatively high
my regards …
Ahmed Masawa
@AhmadMesawa
Vegetarian options: (Soup) Miso Soup
Parking: There is no parking

One of the best Indian restaurants to dine in.The kerala dishes such as beef fry,beef chatty curry(clay pot curry),fish curry,chicken pepper fry goes great with their super fluffy paratha,soft idiyappam and puttu.They have a yummy assortment of Arabic dishes as well.The chicken madfoon served with a flavour full marinated chicken along with Arabic rice springled with fried dry fruits,pomogranete seeds and a side dish of spicy Tomato chilly chutney,salad,cocunut mint chutney,and papad is super yum.The mutton Mandi also has large and tender piece of mutton served warm Mandi rice,spicy chutney,salad and papad.Thier lunch thali options served in banana leaf is also great.The Kerala style pothi choru (rice,fish curry,omlete,fish fry, chutney all wrapped in banana leaf) is amazing too All in all panoor always serves food justifying the price you pay.A nice family joint in Al khor

This restaurant has been a go to place for me and my friends for almost 8 years now to get great Turkish food. They have great selection of barbeques and kebabs. The bbq chicken is very juicy and their shwarma with sauces too hits the perfect note. The appetizers too are well made and garnished. A special mention for their buhaari rice as it's certainly unique to this restaurant and haven't had such taste in any other Turkish restaurant in Qatar.
The ambience isn't fancy, however is kept clean and hygienic. They have a separate small section for families too.
The service is quick and pleasant. They bring your orders to your car too for take away. Lastly , Tahsim and Saif , the owners are more like friends and eager to serve you good food with smile just like their father did few years ago. Do visit for good Turkish food. You will not be left disappointed.
Wheelchair accessibility: Wheelchair can't access

*the white sauce you see on the pizza is ranch sauce I added myself

column9: This is a bit more of an upscale atmosphere. On Sundays they have a buffet where you order it, then they make it and bring it to you. It is recommended to make a reservation, and they will ask if you have one. I wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking to indulge in authentic Japanese & Korean cuisine in the heart of Doha.

One of the most popular Italian restaurants in Doha, Sasso in the beautifully designed Al Hazm Mall. The outdoor seating are fantastic and can be used year round because of the outdoor air conditioning.
We started off with a classic Sasso Caesar Salad, topped with juicy pieces of chicken breast, simple yet delicious. Also tried their Burrata Salad with a delicious special balsamic glaze sauce, highly recommend!
For the next course we got the Eggplant Parmagina, tender pieces of eggplant topped with lots of tomato sauce and cheese. As well as the Sasso Chicken Pesto Roll, a different take on the classic pizza, it's rectangle shaped cut into pieces that you can top with arugala and roll it for easy bites. The pesto sauce was super delicious, but the bread but a bit undercooked for me.
For the main course, we ordered the most popular item, the Pasta Al Forno, fusilli pasta in a pink sauce mixed with chicken, mushroom and lots of cheese. A classic pasta taste, nice for sharing. Also tried their Porcini Asparagus Risotto, creamy sauce and perfect combination with the asparagus and mushroom.
Food: 8/10
Price: 6/10
Location: 10/10
Recommend:
Burrata Salad
Eggplant Parmagina
Pasta Al Forno
Porcini Asparagus Risotto

I visited this restaurant multiple times while in Doha.  They offer a fantastic daily deal on their all-you-can-eat buffet, which I thoroughly enjoyed.  After my second visit, the staff provided a coupon card.  I collected all the stamps and received a discount on my final visit, making for a unique experience.
The food quality is impressive for an all-you-can-eat restaurant, especially for both Korean and Japanese cuisine.  (Dont expect too much.  After all, this is all-you-can-eat restaurant.  But they are good at what they do)  I particularly enjoyed their brisket, sushi, maki, and occasionally indulged in a Japanese hot pot.  Needless to say, I sampled the entire range of what they had to offer.  Each dish was a delightful exploration of flavors, making every meal memorable.
My only regret is not taking more photos to capture these delicious moments.

I went twice during February. Once during their valentine's special set menu with my parents, and the other just on a regular day with friends.
On the valentine's day it was busy so its understandable there were some delays during their servings.
Overall it was lovely and our server Ms. Rogelyn was very accomodating, bring our dishes and answering any questions about the food.
The decorations for valentine's was very pretty there were balloons, roses and petals if requested and even heart confetti.
Their set menu was very generous, having an apetiser, meat bbq, sushi, and dessert.
The food quality was delicious and even if there was some delays in serving due to the busyness this did not impact.
My partner and mother-in-law who's first time it was trying Yeehwa were very impressed and want to visit again.
The other time I went with my friend was a quiet dinner, we had a-la-carte bbq set since it was not bbq buffet day.
This is a generous serving portion for 2, possibly even 3 people since you can choose a dish or a set of sushi roll to go with it.
Our server Ms. Marge was very sweet and accomodating as she helped us navigate the new menu, which had some price changes but worth it.
She also helped with installing and registering the new app for points and registering there to claim for next time.
A very useful thing for frequent Yeehwa visitors. Overall 10/10 experience with a great staff!

Really had high expectations of this place but unfortunately was let down. We sat down and it took 15 minutes for any waiter to notice us, and we were the ones to call on someone, really bad and slow service. We ordered the vine leaves and stuffed dried eggplants, they came to our table in literally 1 minute, they were cold and very dry, unfortunately one of the best and most famous appetizers of any Turkish restaurant wasn't good at all, bad first impression. We got some yogurt & cucumber and mutabal, they were nice, nothing special. The bread was really nice, hot and fluffy yet with crispy edges. We also got the Nurdagi salad which had some tomato, onion, parsley, pomegranate and walnuts topped with lemon juice and pomegranate molasses but it was too light of a dressing and not very pomegranate tasting. It was an okay salad, definitely not like we're used to from other Turkish restaurants. For the main course we tried the Salted Roasted Chicken (whole chicken on top of rice). They served it as a show with fire on the salt and cracked it open. Unfortunately a very sad dish, bland chicken and rice, nothing special at all for 350QR... And it was salted roasted, but didn't taste of salt at all, in fact the dish was covered with soil and then salt was put on top of it, so the salt was all just for show. In turkey we are used to having the actual chicken covered with salt and baked, so the chicken absorbs the salt and retains its moisture to be juicy and moist, but this wasn't the case. Because of this I will not be coming back.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Jwala Restaurant in Doha, and it was an exceptional experience from start to finish. The first thing that struck me was the excellent staff. They were incredibly attentive, friendly, and knowledgeable about the menu, making sure every guest felt welcome and well-cared-for.
The portions were impressively large, providing great value for money. Each dish was not only generous but also beautifully presented, reflecting the restaurant's commitment to quality and authenticity.

Overall, Jwala Restaurant is a must-visit for anyone craving an outstanding Indian dining experience in Doha.

In conclusion, SeñorRitas Tex Mex in Lusail is a must-visit for Tex-Mex enthusiasts and anyone looking for a memorable dining experience. The combination of exceptional food, fantastic drinks, welcoming ambiance, and attentive service makes it a standout choice in the area. I'll definitely be returning for more Tex-Mex delights at SeñorRitas.

Ill start with we had an amazing waitor, who was super kind, understanding and agreed with my complaints. They were also confused on why the owners chose a much more greedy system, he said they only did it for the World Cup but I would still avoid this place. You have to guess what you're gonna pay before you even go inside and they give you coupons for what you pre pay. Once inside you're greeted with a completely different menu from the website and its extremely limited with hiked up prices. Tex-Mex staples like chips & salsa and even queso dip is not avaliable. Had a server who got chips and salsa for me but charged me 50 QR which is ≈15 USD and it tasted like tomato soup with sugar. Got a beef fajita imagining it would be like a tex-mex fajita for more than one however it was not, it cost 100 QR which is roughly ≈33 USD. It tasted okay more like 'sweetened Indian food', yet lacking in seasoning and spices. The business model is inefficient and greedy. A standard margarita is 50 QR as well and its like a shot with heavy flavoring the only thing i had that had any sort if flavor at all to it, to refill would be another 50 QR. While this is a bar, we were told at the entrance you are not allowed to just come have a drink you have to buy food at their raised and greedy prices. I highly recommend avoiding this place if you want to make your money go further and have a quality food experience with the desire for tex-mex, it is the furthest from it. Paying up front at the door is necessary because once you sit inside and experience it you're more inclined to stay because you already paid. The only thing this place offers is overpriced alcohol which is difficult to find in Doha. The location, building and atmosphere is a really cool and beautiful, however, I could recommend much better establishments for alcohol & tex-mex food at better prices.

I wasn’t thrilled by the food, and was surprised to know that this is the most well know Afghani restaurant in Doha, since the food didn’t seem like it.
First, they serve a spicy soup, which I liked. We ordered Foul, Moutabel (an eggplant dip), and Boukhari Rice. The Moutabel was delicious, zero mistakes. However, the rice and Foul didn’t meet my expectations. They lacked the punch of flavor. For dessert, we got these deep fried balls dipped in a sugar syrup. It tasted unfresh, I highly don’t recommend them.
Aside from that, the staff are nice and respond very quickly, and the food is severed quite fast. The atmosphere is so classic for an Afghani restaurant.

The gravy was just okay nothing wow and all the dushes had less salt in taste. Overall we were a group of 8 where we did not enjoy the food at all. We had ordered almost 6 dishes but did not enjoy any.
The staff it friendly,the atmosphere is good and it has live music. But being a restaurant if the food you order does not have the taste, quality and quantity with the a high end price the rest just fades.

From the moment I entered, the ambiance of the restaurant captivated me. The elegant decor, combined with soft lighting, created a soothing and inviting atmosphere.
I had an opportunity to meet Mr Prem Kumar chef such a gem of a person who is in hot kitchen we can see the love and kindness in his cooking.
The highlight of my visit was undoubtedly the delicious sushi that I savored. Each piece was expertly crafted, showcasing the chef's attention to detail and culinary skill. The flavors were exquisite, and the freshness of the ingredients was evident in every bite. Sushi Library truly delivered a remarkable dining experience in terms of taste and presentation.
During my visit, I had the pleasure of being served by Rebecca and Nikitas. Their service was impeccable, and they went above and beyond to ensure that my dining experience was flawless. They were attentive, knowledgeable about the menu, and provided excellent recommendations. Their warm and friendly demeanor made me feel welcome and well taken care of throughout the meal.
Furthermore, the choice of music played in the background added to the overall ambiance. The soothing melodies created a relaxing atmosphere, allowing me to fully enjoy my dining experience. It complemented the elegant setting and enhanced the overall enjoyment of the meal.
In conclusion, Sushi Library in Vendome Mall, Qatar, exceeded my expectations with its delectable sushi, inviting ambiance, and exceptional service provided by Rebecca and Nikitas. All you can eat sushi + miso soup for only 99QR at Soy Tokyo in Place Vendome every Sunday. The price was certainly intriguing and I was pleasantly surprised by the quality and taste of all the sushi I tried. Would definitely be coming back!
You can select as many sushi dishes as you want from the menu, except for the sashimi. The Maki rolls and speciality rolls come in 4 or 8 pieces, and the sushi (nigiri) come in 2 pieces. We tried a bunch of different rolls and they were all delicious. My favorite rolls were the Spicy Tuna Roll, Salmon Avocado Roll, Beef Teriyaki Roll and Shifudo Roll (salmon, tuna, avocado and spicy mayo). Also quite enjoyed their Spider Roll (Soft Shell Crab with Asparagus) and Tsunami Roll (Prawn Tempura, Salmon, Cream Cheese, Avocado in a deep fried roll).
All the fish tasted super fresh and did not have a pungent fishy taste or smell at all. Special mention to their nigiri, especially the salmon and shrimp, the rice was tasty and slightly sweet. The one roll I didn't like was their Diablo Roll, Prawn tempura roll served with crabstick salad on top and mayonnaise, it was a bit too much mayonnaise for me so didn't quite enjoy it.
Their menu is extensive so I would want to come again to try some of their other non sushi items like Ramen and Teriyaki.

Location: 8/10

This place is iconic, and for good reason. There is a serious level of dedication to the flavors produced here and every item on the menu was designed to make those flavors hit your taste buds.
It’s technically a “Japanese” style of menu, but it’s fused with a pretty modern set of items that can suit anyone. They have sushi items, burgers, fish dishes, octopus, noddles etc. you won’t get bored.
It is non alcoholic so keep this in mind - you’re there for the food and atmosphere anyway!
A must try is the coal dish.
The wait times can be problematic in the evenings, they do not accept reservations and so from 7pm onwards you’re basically on a wait list. The line seems to move pretty fast though.
Ask the staff for recommendation, they are super helpful and kind.
You’re going to have to go in with a specific budget in mind depending on the experience you’re looking for, so here is a bit of a guide:
1- two/three friends just hanging out over a few bites - AED150-200
2- four hungry people that want to feel satisfied but not overly full - AED550 - 600
3- five people or more that want to try at least 8 items (some special menu some regular menu) and feel satisfied - AED900 - 1,000
4- best culinary experience to try as many of the menu items as possible and feel satisfied - AED1,200+
Of course you can tailor your experience as you like, but it’s worth trying some of the staple basics as in the pictures I posted (all of that was approx AED 900, but we doubled up on some of those dishes and got drinks).

Parking: Parking was a little troublesome, however we find a spot on the side street next to the restaurant.

This was one of my best food experiences in Jeddah. We had no reservation, so we had to wait for a traditional setting to be available.
We ordered the following:
- Haemul Ramyeon (SR 55) - Noodle soup made with special seasoning in vegetable broth with seafood and vegetables
- Haemul Dolsot Bibimbap (SR 85) - Hot stone pot bibimbap with stir-fried seafood and vegetables in rice mixed with savory soy sauce
- Charcoal-Galbi Kimchi Fried Rice (SR 70) - Kimchi fried rice with charcoal grilled beef short-ribs marinated in BBQ sauce | Served with today's soup
- Korean fried chicken boneless (SR 70) - Sweet and spicy (Yangnyeom)
- Kimchi-Jeon (SR 70) - Spicy cabbage kimchi Korean pancake
- Galbi-Gui (SR 95) - Grilled marinated short-ribs with soy sauce and ground vegetables, fruits
Every order was a delight! The portions were generous, the cooking was top-notch, and the overall experience was simply fantastic. You are served with a complementary soup & salad, and dessert at the end of the meal.
The staff, with their warm and helpful nature, added to the charm of the place. Despite the slightly higher prices, the experience was definitely worth it.

Everything was so delicious and full of flavor. If you know a thing or two about korean food, you'll definitely enjoy the experience. One thing I didn't like was that there was music while it was on Friday. It shouldn't be played specially on a holy day. My recommendation:
1. If you're 4 people, reserve the private room, you'll enjoy it. It has more privacy and it's quieter than other tables.
2. Vege ramyeon, kimbap, and fried chicken with sweet and spicy sauce are a must. The ramyeon is a bit spicy with a slight kimchi taste, and the broth was so warm and had so much flavor. The fried chicken was so juicy and the sauce was so good as well.
3. Staff are very welcoming and gave us two complimentary appetizers and a dessert.
I'll definitely come back again!

Embarking on a culinary journey to this local gem, I was immediately taken by the quality and authenticity of the food offered. Among the standout dishes, the falafel sandwich, generously drizzled with extra tahini, was a revelation. The falafel itself was perfectly crisp on the outside while remaining tender and flavorful within, a testament to the chef’s mastery over traditional cooking techniques. The tahini added a creamy, nutty layer that complemented the falafel beautifully, elevating the sandwich to a memorable delight.
The hummus served was another highlight, embodying the perfect balance of creamy texture and rich flavors, with a subtle hint of garlic and a generous pour of olive oil. It was the kind of hummus you’d find yourself craving at odd hours, a perfect representation of the cuisine’s simplicity and depth.
But it was the Shawarma Laham Sahen that truly captured my heart. The dish was a magnificent array of tender, marinated meat, expertly cooked to retain all its juices and flavors. Paired with fresh vegetables and spices, each bite was a testament to the authentic culinary heritage this restaurant prides itself on.
This dining experience was not just about the food; it was a deep dive into authentic culinary artistry. Each dish was a story, told through spices, textures, and aromas that lingered long after the meal was over. For those in search of genuine flavors and meticulously prepared dishes, this restaurant is a treasure waiting to be discovered.

Decided to dine here on a weekday and it wasn’t crowded but we had booked in advance just in case.. we were warmly greeted by their staff and manager.. staff behavior was top notch from the moment you enter till you leave.
We ordered their Chicken Biryani, Chicken Tandoori, Kebab Khashkhash and Kebab Orfali. Everything was very generously served and in a matter of 10-15 mins, made to order which was very impressive as one can tell apart from reheated and fresh foods. The Biryani is one of the best I’ve had at an intercontinental restaurant. The kebabs were super juicy and made of high quality meats. For desserts, we got their brownie and lotus desserts which were presented beautifully, although I felt the cakes were a bit dry, could’ve been for the sauces to not make them soggy but just for personal preference, it seemed a bit hard.
Overall, a 5/5 food experience that became 10/10 because of the impeccable ambiance and service. Definitely an underrated spot and my best kept secret until more people start discovering it :)

I had an amazing time at the Viking Restaurant, where I felt like I was transported to the medieval era of the Norse warriors. The restaurant is beautifully decorated with authentic Viking artifacts, weapons, and costumes. Our server Valeri was great, he made sure we had everything we needed and gave us some interesting facts about the Viking culture. The fire dancing lady, Maria, was also great, she mesmerized us with her skills and grace. The restaurant offers a variety of dishes from the sea and land, as well as a special Viking meal for two, which includes a selection of their best dishes and drinks. We were a group of eight and we all had a blast. The prices are reasonable for the quality and quantity of the food and the service. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone who loves history, culture, and great food. It is a unique and unforgettable experience that you don't want to miss. Skal!

3 Fils is currently ranked #6 best restaurant in the MENA region, and it did not disappoint. If you live in Dubai or ever visit, you have to try this restaurant located in the lovely Jumeirah Fishing Harbour.
The restaurant serves Japanese food with smaller portions, so it’s nice to share as a group. To start off we got the Salmon Carpaccio, super light and refreshing with lime and sesame oil. Then the Tampachi Tataki, refreshing as well but felt it was a very mild flavor. Also got the Hokkaido Scallops, interesting flavor with the mandarin pieces and sumac.
Next we got the Spicy Beef Tartare, wow what a dish! Served with toasted sourdough bread, the tartare was literally like butter and had the perfect amount of spice. Then we tried the Charcoal, it’s a surprise as mentioned in the menu so don’t want to ruin it, but it was a vegetarian dish served with a lovely sauce. The Charcoal is served on literal charcoal pieces and the exterior was tough similar to charcoal, nice experience. My absolute favorite dish of the meal were the wings topped with soy garlic and togarashi spices. The chicken was super moist with a crispy, sweet and spicy skin, highly recommend.
For the sushi round, we tried 3 different sushi rolls. One thing that 3 Fils is keen on is that they don’t serve soy sauce. Volcano Roll would be my favorite from the ones we tried, came with salmon teriyaki with gochujang sauce. Next the Crispy Eel, which was unique as the rice was separate from the eel, so you needed to combine them yourself to enjoy it together. Then the Spicy Tuna Roll, for me the texture was off, it was super mushy. But the flavor was nice, served with samjang, spicy Korean paste and wasabi mayo.
For the main we had the 72 hour Lamb Ribs, a must order dish that fell of the bone effortlessly and tasted delicious. Also a must try is the Indomie, Yes Indomie, which came with beef chorizo, broccoli and snap peas. The flavor was incredible, mostly from the oils of the beef chorizo.
For dessert, another dish that you need to try was the Karak Ice Cream. It was plated table side with a bit of a show. The main part was the karak flavored ice cream, tasted just like karak and I really liked it. It was served with a milk foam cream and drizzled with butterscotch as well as a black tea crumble. Very strong flavors that went so well with each other.
Food: 9/10
Price: 8/10
Location: 8/10

This is a popular eatery in Zamalek and we had to wait for a table to be seated. That said there are only 4 or 5 tables in the restaurant, should one want to sit in. Take-out option is available.
In a normal day I would give this establishment a 5 star review, however, it merits only  4 stars on this visit.
We had to wait around to be seated, which is acceptable under current circumstances. Once we were seated the aircon dripped onto our backs. This again we could overlook as at least the condensation didn't flavor the food. My only disappointment was my choice of food the koshary was not the best I have ever eaten. It was premixed and not separately served, presumably to save space and the chef ran out of fried onions.
All in all the prices are fair and the food comes out fast. Seeing the popularity, maybe there is a need for a larger venue or expansion of this one.

We ordered yangnyeom chicken (deep fried chicken with korean chili barbecue) , Hwa bulgogi (grilled beef with korean barbecue), and jajang myeon (black soybeans noodle with beef), and sangria.
The chicken is our favorite, it is crispy and not oily, the beef tasted really fresh and perfectly seasoned, sangria was refreshing. We will definitely come back again.

Visited this place yesterday after becoming fed up of the same old duplicate post lockdown menus that have infected many restaurants in Jeddah. Hidden away next to Burt's on rawdah Street... This place was amazing... From the intimate venue and authentic cuisine... To the excellent service. The food was excellent with portions that generally catered for two people which mitigates the  prices which are more expensive than your typical casual dining spot. If you like the flavour and textures of Chinese food but with the quality dial turned up to 10 then Sura is definitely the place to be.
UPDATE: 30.12.2022
as a customer of this restaurant for years myself and my friends have spent literally thousands of riyals on food at this establishment and the quality and consistency had been second to none. Unfortunately this seems to now be consigned to the past. I visited today and it seems a change of chef has resulted in food that is a shadow of what it used to be. I ordered the signature bulgogi and was disappointed to find it fatty and mixed with vegetables. I also ordered a chicken dish which felt way below the standard that this restaurant used to uphold. If all of this didn't add up to a bad enough experience, I was about to be shocked by the worst restaurant manager I have ever encountered in this city. On complaining to the manager called 'jung' I found him to be dismissive and obnoxious... Offering no apology and walking off mid conversation after stating that the food we had was more authentically Korean than what they had previously offered.... As if that subjective 'fact' was supposed to make me feel better about the unpleasant food that I had half eaten. Needless to say, sura lost themselves a patron today... As I will not be going back... And I advise readers to avoid this place unless you are intent on witnessing a master class in poor customer service.

Went for a work lunch and truly ordered too much for the two of us (not a skinny girl lunch). The raw dishes were delicious, scallops incredibly fresh with the right sauce blend and the citrusy kick complemented it well. I’m a huge fan of greens and salads so we went with the signature one and it was fresh, had a bit of crunch and wasn’t dense in seaweed flavour, really enjoyed it. The tempura tuna nori was incredible, was so full by this point but it was probably my favourite.
The sushi was decent but I felt it was too busy, I prefer the simpler sushi dishes so you can taste the freshness of the sashimi. We ordered the shrimp tempura and the spicy tuna, prawn was my preferred out of the two. If I went again I’d just opt for the raw dishes and the salads, they were really tasty. Skipped dinner afterwards.
Also, staff were really lovely and let us sit for the full afternoon. It was beautiful weather and so nice ti be next to the water.
Parking: It was just super busy.
Kid-friendliness: Kid friendly sushi on the menu plus easy sitting and casual atmosphere.

Bucketlist gastronomic experience! Pinch me! What a pleasure to visit this top level establishment. Michelin star yet casual, right in the jetty and a hive of activity. The sun was out but there was a chill in the breeze. No issues, out came the pashmimas to drape over the shoulders. Now the food...
Clean, fresh combinations focusing on the star ingredient in each dish. We ordered about 5 plates between 3 of us. Very affordable so we didn't need to take out a 2nd mortgage. We could easily have ordered more, but we didn't want to ruin the experience by feeling stuffed and honestly, we wanted to try those desserts! We ordered 3. We demolished every morsel. Beautifully plated without being OTT, excellent ingredients, perfect ambiance. Faultless.. I couldn't ask for anything more. I cannot wait to return.
Kid-friendliness: Surprising and unusual kiddy options

By far my favorite restaurant in Dubai, and such a bowl of fresh air from the global brands and their too often stale menus dished out in multi million dollar interiors.
At the 3 Fils, it’s all about thought provoking modern, urban, Japanese dishes, unlikely and yet precisely controlled combination of taste and texture profiles that suggest that an artistic and creative mind has been hard at work in the kitchen to come up with a culinary journey that is intent on leaving you with lasting memories. This food focused approach is underlined by the fact that this establishment, thankfully not attached to a hotel complex, is therefore not licensed for alcohol. Fear not, the wonderfully unique mocktails entirely make up for it. And the fact that the gems, skilfully executed by a resolutely inspired kitchen team, are served by an enthusiastic, energetic and definitely friendly front of house team, is certainly the cherry on the proverbial cake. I will always return here with the high expectations that my very first experience allowed me to build and that subsequent visits ever since reinforced

The dining experience and atmosphere during Eid were outstanding. Despite not having a reservation, they promptly seated us outside overlooking the marina. The drinks were expertly crafted with minimal sugar, and we enjoyed freshly baked bread. The chicken samosas were uniquely delicious with pine seed stuffing and served with a flavorful sauce. The whole grilled chicken was tender and perfectly cooked, though the portion size was quite generous for one person, suitable for sharing among three. While the lamb kebabs were juicy and flavorful, I noticed a distinct aroma typical of lamb meat, which some restaurants manage to mitigate effectively. I'm uncertain if this applies to all lamb dishes, as I've dined at restaurants where this aroma is not noticeable. Some might find the typical lamb aroma slightly off-putting. Despite this, the portions were generous, and the service was exceptional. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone seeking a fine dining experience in Qatar.

Yasmine Palace has to be one of the most beautiful restaurants we have ever visited!
The location on The Pearl is stunning with indoor and outdoor seating available and beautiful twinkling lights everywhere. We chose to dine outdoors as it was a beautiful warm evening in December (being from the UK, this was a real treat!)
We had been craving kunefa whilst on holiday so our hotel concierge recommended we try here and we were so glad that we did.
It took us around 10mins in a taxi to get here from the city centre and once we arrived and saw the opulent restaurant, we knew we were in for a treat!
For such a vast restaurant, the service we received was efficient, professional and friendly. I have to particularly mention our waiters Devakee and Amit who were great. Also, the restaurant manager Wael Hamdan was so warm, welcoming and helpful that I wish all hospitality staff could be this way! Thank you for your kindness- it was very much appreciated.
The food was outstanding and we loved the complimentary appetisers that were brought out to us on a golden serving dish… breads, crackers, vegetables and several different types of hummus- all absolutely delicious and a wonderful way to start our meal and get our tastebuds tingling. We were also given 2 small glasses of fruit juices served in delightful crystal glasses which were very refreshing and a great palate cleanser.
My husband and I opted for several dishes to share including cheese samosas, hummus with meat, moussaka and grilled halloumi - it was all heavenly and we really couldn’t decide which dish we enjoyed the most as it was all fantastic.

For me, this is one of the best public spots in Qatar.
First, it's free.
Second, the view is sooo nice especially at sunset to evening. Also, during winter, as you will feel the cool breeze of the air brushing through your face. From sea view to city lights, im sure you will enjoy it.
Third, the place offers a nice area for running, jogging,walking and strolling with your kids, family or friends.
Lastly, it has clean, accessible and fancy toilets. (I will not spoil about it so make sure you will drop by at their toilet to figure out why 😉).
P.S Make sure to walk up to the end of it and you'll be surprise what you will see.

Yemeni food enthusiasts, rejoice! This restaurant is a hidden gem for indulging in authentic Yemeni cuisine. Prepare your taste buds for a delightful journey with two must-try dishes: Lahsa Eggs and Fahsa Meat. Lahsa Eggs are a delightful blend of eggs, cheese, and tomato that creates an explosion of flavors in your mouth. Meanwhile, Fahsa Meat, simmered in its rich sauce, is a savory delight that will leave you craving for more.
To complete this culinary adventure, pair these dishes with their Yemeni bread, generously sized and perfect for savoring every bite. If you’re feeling particularly hungry, don’t miss out on their tantalizing offerings like Hanid Meat or Borma Meat; I personally tried these and was thoroughly impressed.
What sets this dining experience apart is the picturesque setting near the beach, allowing you to relish your meal while soaking in the mesmerizing blue hues of the ocean. If you opt for a nighttime visit, the pleasant weather adds to the charm. This restaurant truly offers a perfect combination of delectable Yemeni cuisine and a captivating ambiance that will keep you coming back for more.

The ambience seamlessly blends coastal charm with authentic Yemeni warmth, creating a dining experience that transcends the ordinary. The menu boasts a symphony of flavors, but the must-try items are the chai meat mokalkal—a savory delight that tantalizes the taste buds—and the shakshouka, a dish that perfectly marries bold spices with fresh, sea-kissed ingredients. From the captivating sea view to the exceptional culinary offerings, this restaurant promises a journey of taste and atmosphere that is truly unforgettable.
